The strategy is remarkably ingenious. One need not persuade ordinary citizens that billionaires deserve greater power if one can convince them that the gravest threats to their liberty emanate from journalists, immigrants, feminists, liberals and minorities. Public resentment is redirected away from economic exploitation and towards manufactured cultural antagonisms. Citizens are encouraged to wage interminable battles over identity while the architects of their economic circumstances pursue their interests with remarkably little interference.

Religion and identitarian politics have become indispensable instruments in this enterprise. Sections of America’s religious right have increasingly been conscripted into a political movement that conflates Christianity with a particular strain of conservative nationalism. Political allegiance becomes a litmus test of religious authenticity. A politician’s personal depravity, dishonesty, questionable business practices or indifference to the vulnerable becomes inconsequential when measured against his professed willingness to wage war against designated cultural enemies.

The contradiction is staggering. A billionaire can amass extraordinary wealth, bankroll politicians committed to dismantling regulatory safeguards and nevertheless emerge as an exalted champion of Christian civilisation. Religious rhetoric provides a convenient moral imprimatur for political and economic interests that might otherwise struggle to survive sustained public scrutiny.

Race and identity serve a comparable purpose. Rather than encourage citizens to interrogate the beneficiaries of existing economic arrangements, political operatives redirect their anxieties towards those supposedly imperilling their cultural identity. Immigrants become convenient scapegoats. Diversity is recast as persecution. Universities are portrayed as incubators of ideological contamination. Journalists become enemies of the people. Every disagreement is elevated into an existential confrontation over the fate of civilisation.

The objective is not necessarily to persuade everyone. It is to keep everyone perpetually antagonised. Meanwhile, the billionaires remain comfortably removed from the battlefield, financing the combatants and appropriating the spoils.

Peter Thiel offers perhaps one of the most illuminating illustrations of this phenomenon.

Thiel has been travelling the world delivering supposedly secret lectures warning of the advent of the Antichrist. Within his apocalyptic worldview, those advocating restrictions on artificial intelligence and questioning the unchecked proliferation of data centres appear to occupy a particularly troubling position. Imagine the irony: a billionaire technology investor whose financial interests could be imperilled by regulatory intervention is invoking religious imagery to shape public sentiment against those demanding greater accountability. What more effective recruitment strategy could there be than portraying one’s economic critics as agents of biblical destruction?

There is another particularly striking contradiction. Thiel, a gay venture capitalist whose investments and political influence extend into technologies capable of harvesting vast quantities of personal data, facilitating surveillance and expanding the reach of powerful institutions, nevertheless presents himself as humanity’s defender against the biblical Antichrist. The irony is difficult to overlook, particularly given the hostility towards gay rights within sections of the religious political movement with which he has aligned himself.

They have persuaded working people that their principal adversary is not the concentration of wealth but the immigrant competing for employment. That their children’s economic precarity is not connected to structural inequality but to some imaginary liberal conspiracy. That the journalist investigating abuses of power poses a greater threat to civilisation than the billionaire financing the politician responsible for those abuses. This is political misdirection elevated to an art form.

It is an ingenious exercise in redefining the terms of public discourse. Instead of asking whether powerful technology corporations should be subjected to meaningful regulatory oversight, the public is invited to contemplate whether those demanding such oversight are obstructing humanity’s salvation. Religion is thus repurposed as a sophisticated instrument of commercial and political self-preservation.

The architecture of this influence deserves closer examination. Billionaires finance the politicians who appoint judges, shape regulatory priorities and determine the direction of public policy. They acquire or invest in media platforms capable of amplifying congenial narratives and discrediting inconvenient journalism. They nurture religious and cultural grievances that keep their political constituencies emotionally invested. When accountability threatens to intrude, they can summon formidable battalions of lawyers, lobbyists and political allies to frustrate or neutralise its consequences.

Their political lapdogs provide the legislative cover, judicial appointments and ideological justification. The media machinery manufactures the narrative. Religion supplies the moral vocabulary. Identity politics furnishes the foot soldiers. And the public is left preoccupied with the wrong battles.

This is how billionaires acquire the practical privileges of being above the law without necessarily dismantling the legal system itself. Their ambition is considerably more sophisticated: to influence who enforces the law, whose conduct attracts scrutiny, which violations become matters of public concern and which institutions are sufficiently debilitated to look the other way.

The statutes remain intact, but their enforcement becomes increasingly selective. Democratic institutions continue to function, but their independence is progressively compromised. The outward appearance of accountability is preserved even as its substance is hollowed out.

Perhaps the most consequential achievement of these billionaire-backed movements is not that they have persuaded ordinary people to admire billionaires. It is that they have persuaded ordinary people to defend political and economic arrangements that disproportionately enrich billionaires, frequently at the expense of their own material interests.

They have persuaded working people that their principal adversary is not the concentration of wealth but the immigrant competing for employment. That their children’s economic precarity is not connected to structural inequality but to some imaginary liberal conspiracy. That the journalist investigating abuses of power poses a greater threat to civilisation than the billionaire financing the politician responsible for those abuses. This is political misdirection elevated to an art form.

These billionaires understand something their critics occasionally underestimate: power is not sustained by financial resources alone. It is sustained by the narratives through which people determine who deserves authority, who threatens their existence and who possesses the credentials to rescue them.

They have mastered the architecture of that storytelling. They have transmuted wealth into political leverage, political leverage into media dominance and media dominance into an imposing protective shield against accountability.

They have not merely purchased politicians. They have helped acquire the very narrative within which those politicians operate. And that, more than anything else, is how they won the messaging war.

Osmund Agbo is a medical doctor, author, and the 2026 recipient of the Thabo Mbeki Prize for Scholarship and Public Service.

World.title: Katsina 2027: When military discipline meets politics, By Mukhtar Ya’u Madobi
World.content:
Musa’s effectiveness will therefore depend on adapting his experience to an environment driven by voluntary participation and public confidence.

As political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 general elections, Katsina State is emerging as a battleground between the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). Beyond political personalities and campaign promises, the contest will test leadership, grassroots mobilisation and strategic communication.

At the centre of the PDP’s renewed ambition are its governorship candidate, Senator Garba Yakubu Lado Danmarke, and Brigadier General Sagir Musa (Rtd.), a former Nigerian Army spokesperson appointed director-general of the party’s Governorship Campaign Council.

Musa’s appointment brings military discipline, organisational leadership and public communication experience into the PDP’s campaign machinery. His ability to translate these competencies into political mobilisation could significantly influence the party’s electoral prospects.

On 14 November, Senator Danmarke inaugurated the campaign council, alongside 17 other committees comprising more than 2,000 professionals, political stakeholders and volunteers. The structures were established to coordinate electoral activities across Katsina’s 34 local government areas.

The inauguration at the PDP state headquarters in Katsina signalled the opposition party’s determination to strengthen grassroots structures and challenge the APC’s dominance.

Barely four days later, on 18 November, the PDP formally flagged off its governorship campaign, unveiling candidates for the three senatorial districts, 15 House of Representatives constituencies, and 34 State House of Assembly seats.

Addressing supporters, General Musa pledged effective coordination and collaboration.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“With the trust and responsibility placed on my shoulders by our leader, Senator Lado, I will leave no stone unturned. We will work in collaboration with all stakeholders in the party to ensure victory,” he declared.

The early mobilisation demonstrates organisational enthusiasm, although converting campaign crowds into electoral support will require sustained engagement, credible policies and effective grassroots coordination.

Beyond political mobilisation, the PDP campaign has outlined priorities addressing Katsina’s development challenges.

General Musa identified agriculture and security as central to Senator Danmarke’s proposed agenda.

On agriculture, the candidate plans to promote mechanised farming by improving farmers’ access to affordable tractors and modern equipment. Such interventions could enhance productivity, strengthen food security and improve rural livelihoods.

However, mechanisation must be accompanied by financing, irrigation, extension services, equipment maintenance and access to markets.

Security remains particularly critical in Katsina, where banditry, kidnapping and attacks on communities have disrupted agriculture, commerce and education.

Drawing on his military experience, Musa advocates a combination of conventional security operations and socio-economic interventions.

He identified poverty and unemployment as vulnerabilities requiring attention through skills acquisition, economic empowerment and access to start-up capital.

He also emphasised modern security equipment, personnel training, intelligence gathering and collaboration between security agencies and communities.

This approach recognises that sustainable security requires coordinated enforcement, community participation and economic opportunities.

Senator Danmarke similarly identified insecurity, declining educational standards, unemployment, poverty, agricultural challenges and inadequate roads and healthcare facilities as major concerns.

He promised vocational training, business development support and start-up capital for youths and women to encourage entrepreneurship and self-reliance.

Education features prominently in his proposals. He pledged free education to Katsina indigenes, improved learning facilities, adequate instructional materials and qualified teachers.

His supporters cite the Lado Education Development Foundation, established in 2020, which reportedly provided scholarships to more than 35,000 students across universities, polytechnics and colleges of education.

This initiative offers a reference point for assessing his commitment to educational development, although implementing statewide free education would require sustainable financing and institutional capacity.

In healthcare, Danmarke promised modern medical facilities across Katsina’s three senatorial zones and access to free medicines.

“I assure you that if elected, foreign medical tourism will become a thing of the past in Katsina. My administration will establish state-of-the-art medical facilities to address the challenges confronting the health sector. Citizens will also have access to free medicines,” he stated.

He also pledged to address pension payment difficulties affecting retired civil servants.

These commitments are ambitious, but their credibility will depend on realistic financing, implementation timelines and measurable outcomes.

While Danmarke provides the political vision, Musa carries responsibility for translating the campaign’s objectives into an effective electoral structure.

His professional background explains why the PDP entrusted him with this assignment.

In February 2019, Musa, then a Colonel, was appointed Nigerian Army spokesperson by the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Tukur Yusuf Buratai (Rtd.).

He succeeded Brigadier General Sani Usman Kukasheka (Rtd.), having previously served as spokesperson of the Nigerian Army’s 82 Division in Enugu.

His appointment as Director of Army Public Relations placed him at the centre of military communication, media engagement and information management during a period of significant national security challenges.

On 25 November, 2020, the Army Council approved his promotion to Brigadier General alongside 135 other senior officers.

His career involved institutional communication, operational coordination, stakeholder engagement and managing sensitive information under pressure.

These competencies are relevant to political campaigns, where public perception, message consistency, crisis communication and organisational effectiveness influence electoral outcomes.

However, military leadership differs from democratic political organisation. While military institutions emphasise command structures, political campaigns require consultation, persuasion, compromise and accommodation of competing interests.

Musa’s effectiveness will therefore depend on adapting his experience to an environment driven by voluntary participation and public confidence.

Coordinating more than 2,000 campaign officials and volunteers across 34 local government areas requires clear responsibilities, effective communication and mechanisms for resolving disagreements.

It also demands messages tailored to different communities.

Farmers affected by insecurity may prioritise protection and agricultural support, while unemployed graduates seek jobs, entrepreneurs demand financing and pensioners expect prompt payment of benefits.

Musa’s communication experience could help translate Danmarke’s development proposals into messages that resonate with these constituencies.

His security background may also strengthen the campaign’s ability to articulate realistic proposals involving intelligence coordination, institutional responsibilities and community protection.

Nevertheless, professional credentials alone cannot guarantee electoral victory. Their value must be demonstrated through effective organisation, inclusive leadership and measurable results.

The PDP’s early campaign activities have generated enthusiasm, with Senator Danmarke interpreting supporters’ turnout as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the APC.

Yet political rallies are not elections. Large crowds may demonstrate mobilisation capacity without necessarily reflecting broader electoral preferences.

The ruling APC remains a formidable political force in Katsina and deserves the opportunity to defend its record and present competing development programmes.

For the PDP, the challenge is to move beyond criticism and convince voters that its alternatives are practical, affordable and sustainable.

For the APC, the responsibility is to demonstrate achievements, acknowledge outstanding challenges and explain why its leadership should continue.

The contest must be peaceful, allowing every candidate to campaign freely, while voters assess leadership capacity, integrity and development priorities.

Senator Lado Danmarke’s decision to appoint General Sagir Musa is a strategic choice combining political ambition with military experience, institutional coordination and strategic communication.

For Musa, the assignment offers an opportunity to demonstrate that leadership skills acquired through military service can strengthen democratic political organisation.

For Danmarke, the challenge is to convert ambitious promises into a credible development blueprint capable of addressing Katsina’s security, agricultural, educational and economic challenges.

The PDP campaign train has departed, with Senator Lado Danmarke providing the political direction and General Sagir Musa coordinating its movement. But the destination remains uncertain.

Ultimately, victory in 2027 will depend not on military credentials, campaign enthusiasm or political slogans, but on the confidence of Katsina voters in the candidates’ capacity to deliver meaningful development.

Mukhtar Ya’u Madobi writes from Kano.

World.title: EFCC case: ‘I’m most vilified; I shall be vindicated’– Yahaya Bello
World.content:
Yahaya Bello

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has described himself as “the most transparent and the most vilified,” saying he expects to be vindicated over corruption allegations against him.

Bello spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, saying he would not comment on the EFCC case in detail because it was before the courts. He said Kogi State’s budgets, audited accounts, and records of performance were available online and challenged journalists and others to examine them and ask questions under the Freedom of Information Act.

“I’d rather decline to make a comment about EFCC on national television because we’re in court. However, from inception till date, all of our financials and budgets and the performance on the ground are online. We have our eight years’ budget, eight years’ final account, which we call an audited account, and the performance on the ground; we have them online,” he said.

Bello said he had experience managing public resources before becoming governor and was already financially established. He said he granted local governments financial autonomy after taking office and left the allegations for the courts to determine.

“I was never; I never assumed office as a poor man. I’m a man of my means before I assumed the office. God blessed me in my early age, and my children have been schooling in high-profile schools, both in Abuja and abroad. In any case, I don’t think I was a governor that time. The rest, I’ll leave it for them to prove it in court,” he said.

He added, “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. I’m the most transparent. I’m the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated.”

Bello also said he had no regrets about his time as governor and accepted responsibility for what happened during his tenure, adding: “I gave my best.”

The EFCC is prosecuting Bello in two separate cases relating to alleged financial misconduct during his 2016–2024 governorship tenure.

World.title: 2027: NDC candidate pledges inclusive representation for riverine communities
World.content:
By Chancel Bomadi Sunday

The Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta South Senatorial District, Chief Adowei Freedom Binaebi, has pledged to prioritise the needs of riverine communities through inclusive representation if elected in the 2027 general elections.

Binaebi made the pledge on Thursday during a consultation visit to Bomadi, headquarters of Bomadi Local Government Area of Delta State.

He said his decision to contest the senatorial seat was informed by the need to give riverine communities a stronger voice in the National Assembly and ensure that their basic needs received adequate attention.

The candidate also promised to initiate youth capacity-building programmes aimed at equipping young people with relevant skills and addressing poverty in the area.

He appealed to the people of Bomadi to support his ambition, assuring them that he would not disappoint them if elected.

“From all indications, the people are suffering due to the mismanagement in governance, and I have resolved to contest in order to deliver my people from this plight.

“I will ensure inclusive representation for the people of the riverine communities when entrusted with the mandate, and I will never let them down,” he said.

Binaebi urged residents to vote for NDC candidates across elective positions in the 2027 elections, describing such support as necessary to enable the party fulfil its promises.

“I urge the people of Bomadi to cast their votes five over five for the NDC candidates in 2027, and we will honour and fulfil the mandate entrusted to us,” he added.

World.title: Sanwo-Olu targets 2,000 more homes before leaving office
World.content:
Gov Sanwo-Olu

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has pledged to deliver more than 2,000 additional housing units before the end of his tenure in 2027 as part of efforts to address the state’s housing deficit.

The governor made the commitment on Friday while commissioning two residential estates comprising 294 housing units in the Ogombo and Ajah areas of Eti-Osa Local Government Area.

He also called for the speedy passage of the revised Lagos State Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill into law, while promising a four-lane expansion of Ogombo Road to improve access and ease traffic congestion in the area.

Sanwo-Olu disclosed that more than 2,000 housing units developed by the Ministry of Housing were ready for commissioning in Ibeshe, Sangotedo, Egan and Epe.

He added that other housing schemes being undertaken by the Lagos State Development and Property Corporation (LSDPC) were ongoing in Shogunro, Ogba, Apapa and Ogudu.

The governor said government alone could not meet the housing demands of Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre, stressing that his administration was adopting a partnership model involving the provision of land, regulatory oversight and an enabling environment to attract private-sector investment.

The two commissioned projects are the 165-unit Treasure Estate at Ajiwe, Ogombo, developed by LSDPC in partnership with AKF Properties Limited, and the 129-unit Brooks Habitat at Abraham Adesanya, Ajah, facilitated by the Ministry of Housing in partnership with Brook Assets and Resources Limited.

Treasure Estate comprises two-bedroom terrace houses, three-bedroom flats and three-bedroom terrace houses, with facilities including a swimming pool, gymnasium, five-a-side football pitch, jogging tracks, water treatment plant and modern drainage systems.

Brooks Habitat, located on 2.3 hectares of land across 20 blocks, comprises 42 two-bedroom flats, 42 three-bedroom flats with service quarters and 45 three-bedroom terrace houses.

Its facilities include a clinic, gymnasium, solar-powered streetlights, paved access roads and dedicated security.

Addressing infrastructure needs in the rapidly developing Eti-Osa corridor, Sanwo-Olu pledged that Ogombo Road would be expanded into a four-lane carriageway, with improved drainage infrastructure.

He commended the developers, engineers and artisans involved in the projects, saying their contributions had helped deliver housing options across different income categories.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Housing, Moruf Akinderu-Fatai, urged the Lagos State House of Assembly to expedite the passage of the revised Lagos State Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill.

He said a sustainable housing framework required strong legislation to address unfair rental practices and protect the interests of both landlords and tenants.

Providing details of the Ogombo housing scheme, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of LSDPC, Ayodeji Joseph, disclosed that the two-bedroom terrace units were priced at N65 million.

He said prospective buyers could access mortgage facilities through the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) and the Mortgage Refinancing and Infrastructure Fund.

Joseph added that four other housing projects within the axis were nearing completion.

In his response, the Majority Leader of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Noheem Adams, assured residents that the revised tenancy bill would be passed into law “very soon”.

He commended Sanwo-Olu for what he described as tangible housing and infrastructure development across Eti-Osa and other parts of the state.

World.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
World.content:
File image

At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur.

The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday.

“Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said.

He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished.

Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical.

In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra.

In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports.

Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations.

Vanguard News

World.title: Four die, 24 rescued as Bayelsa burial boat capsizes
World.content:
Photo used to illustrate the story

Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday.

Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie.

The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized.

Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa.

He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment.

The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation.

He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders.

Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for.

World.title: UNICEF raises alarm over 624,000 out-of-school children
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised concerns over the high number of out-of-school children in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states, disclosing that about 624,000 children have been identified as being outside the classroom across the three states.

The organisation said although about 68,000 children had benefited from interventions to return them to school, the scale of the challenge required urgent government action, increased investment and stronger community mobilisation.

UNICEF’s Chief of Field Office in Sokoto, Dr Michael Juma, made this known at a media briefing organised by the organisation’s Sokoto Field Office as part of activities marking the 2026 World Children’s Day.

He called for coordinated action by governments, media organisations, traditional institutions, religious leaders and community stakeholders to address challenges confronting children in the region.

Juma urged journalists across the three states to intensify public enlightenment, investigative reporting and advocacy to promote children’s rights, strengthen government accountability and ensure access to education, healthcare, nutrition and other essential services.

Describing the media as a critical partner in advancing children’s rights, he said journalists must go beyond reporting events to exposing gaps in service delivery and holding relevant authorities accountable.

“The media are important duty-bearers in advancing children’s rights. Journalists must provide balanced coverage that highlights development achievements while drawing attention to persistent gaps affecting the wellbeing of children,” he said.

He reaffirmed UNICEF’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with the governments of Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara, development partners, traditional and religious leaders, and grassroots organisations to guarantee children access to quality and inclusive education, healthcare, adequate nutrition, safe drinking water and social protection.

Providing an account of interventions undertaken through UNICEF’s partnerships with the three state governments, Juma disclosed that approximately 98,000 children had benefited from the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) programme, designed to improve foundational literacy and numeracy.

He said the organisation was also supporting teacher professional development, provision of instructional materials, accelerated basic education, integrated Qur’anic education and innovative learning opportunities, including radio-based education and the Nigeria Learning Passport.

According to him, the interventions are particularly targeted at children affected by insecurity, displacement and other emergencies.

On healthcare and immunisation, Juma disclosed that approximately 7.8 million children across the three states had been reached through measles-rubella vaccination, while more than five million children were vaccinated during the last concluded polio immunisation campaign.

He further said Kebbi State had recorded progress in malaria vaccination, with approximately 148,000 children receiving the first dose and 130,000 receiving the second dose.

He stressed that effective healthcare delivery and sustained immunisation campaigns remained essential to reducing preventable childhood deaths and improving children’s survival.

On malnutrition, the UNICEF official commended the Sokoto and Zamfara State Governments for committing approximately N100 million and N500 million respectively towards the procurement of Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), used in treating children suffering from severe acute malnutrition.

He also acknowledged the Kebbi State Government’s contribution of approximately N540 million towards free medical services for children.

Juma highlighted UNICEF-supported social health insurance interventions, which he said had expanded healthcare access to approximately 86,000 beneficiaries in Zamfara, 18,000 in Sokoto and 10,000 in Kebbi.

In the area of child protection, he said UNICEF had supported the development of child protection legislation, Family Court Rules and social protection policies aimed at strengthening the protection, rehabilitation and reintegration of vulnerable children, including those in conflict with the law.

He also highlighted the establishment of a Special Care Baby Unit in Sokoto, with similar interventions being advanced in Kebbi and Zamfara to improve medical attention for premature and low-birth-weight babies.

Despite the interventions, Juma acknowledged that significant challenges remained, particularly the large number of children still excluded from formal education.

He said the gap between the 624,000 children identified as out of school and the approximately 68,000 reached through re-enrolment efforts required urgent government intervention, increased funding and stronger community participation.

“Identifying these children is only the first step. The real challenge is ensuring that they return to school and remain there to acquire the knowledge and skills necessary for their future,” he said.

Addressing concerns over declining international development funding, Juma explained that the financial challenge was a global development issue and not peculiar to Nigeria.

He said UNICEF was intensifying its resource mobilisation strategies to sustain critical interventions and support state governments, assuring that education programmes across the three states had not been affected by the funding decline experienced earlier in the year.

On the difficulties of delivering services in remote and insecurity-affected communities, he said UNICEF was working through government structures, field facilitators and third-party monitoring arrangements to ensure that interventions reached vulnerable children and women.

He called for stronger coordination at ward and local government levels, stressing that protecting children’s rights was a collective responsibility that should not be left to UNICEF or government institutions alone.

“We need the active participation of government agencies, development partners, civil society organisations, traditional and religious leaders, community structures and parents. Journalists must also use their platforms to educate communities, generate demand for essential services and hold stakeholders accountable for their commitments to children,” he said.

As part of efforts to strengthen media participation, Juma invited journalists to join future field visits to document UNICEF-supported projects and independently assess their impact on vulnerable communities.

He also urged media organisations across the three states to support the December 5 to 11, 2026 polio immunisation campaign through public awareness, pre-campaign mobilisation and community engagement to encourage parents and caregivers to present eligible children for vaccination.

The briefing concluded with a renewed call for collective action as the world marks the 2026 World Children’s Day under the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.”

UNICEF maintained that protecting children’s rights must go beyond policy declarations and public commitments to sustained investment, effective service delivery and measurable accountability, warning that the future of the region depended largely on the commitment of its leaders and communities to protect, educate and empower the next generation.

World.title: ‘Issakaba Returns’ grosses N47.8m in opening weekend, sets new record for Nollywood action thriller
World.content:
By Benjamin Njoku

The highly anticipated Nollywood classic, “Issakaba Returns” stormed the domestic box office, recording a spectacular opening weekend gross of N47.8 million to become the highest-grossing debut ever for an action thriller.

The film, directed by popular filmmaker and producer, Lancelot Oduwa Imasuen, premiered last Wednesday at Silverbird Cinemas, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Celebrating the feat, Lancelot, fondly called D’Guvnor, thanked everyone who showed up, bought tickets, filled the cinemas and embraced “Issakaba Returns” with so much love.

“To everyone who has supported this journey, shared the excitement, spread the word and made the opening weekend this remarkable, I do not take your love for granted.

“This is more than numbers. It is a testament to the love, nostalgia and connection you all have with this story.

“N47.8 million opening weekend gross, and this is only the beginning!

“Thank you for believing in us. Thank you for showing up. The love has been organic, and we feel every bit of it,” Lancelot said.

The premiere of “Issakaba Returns” was spectacular and memorable. The evening exploded into war songs, cultural dance and gyration as the film began its cinema run.

Long before the lights went down inside the cinema hall, the carnival had already begun outside. Drummers, dancers and chanting fans set the mood, recreating the fearless spirit of the Issakaba Boys who, 25 years ago, stood against evil in the South-East.

For the lead character, Sam Dede, the return is more than nostalgia. It is a message.

Speaking at the premiere, he said the evils the Issakaba Boys fought a quarter of a century ago, kidnapping, money rituals, human trafficking are still ravaging society today.

First released in 2001 and inspired by real-life vigilante movements, the original “Issakaba” became a cultural phenomenon.

World.title: Davido and Chioma: The love story continues
World.content:
By Benjamin Njoku

Afrobeats superstar Davido is known for flaunting his wife, Chioma Adeleke, on social media, displaying public affection and storming international show venues in her company.

It is no surprise, therefore, that the three-time Grammy nominee has taken their romance to the studio, borrowing a leaf from the likes of Adekunle Gold and Simi, Banky W and Adesuwa Etomi, as well as Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who have all turned their love stories into music.

For Davido, Chioma has never just been his wife. She has been his muse from the very beginning.

Their love story in music started in 2018 with ‘Assurance’, the birthday gift Davido dedicated to Chioma when they were still dating. Chioma starred in the video, and the song became one of the most iconic love anthems in Afrobeats history.

She returned in 2020 for ‘1 Milli’, whose wedding-themed video further celebrated their relationship.

Nearly eight years after ‘Assurance’, ‘Already Falling’ brings that story full circle, from young lovers to husband and wife.

The song, the eighth track on Davido’s sixth studio album, “ORIADÉ”, was released on July 31, 2026. It blends English, Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, and reimagines Elvis Presley’s timeless classic ‘Can’t Help Falling in Love’ through an Afrobeats lens with background vocals by Peruzz

The official video, released on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, stars Chioma as his leading lady once again.

Directed by Meji Alabi, who also directed ‘Assurance, the video was filmed at the historic Château de Chanteloup, the estate of French cognac house Maison Martell in Cognac, France.

It blends French elegance with Nigerian style, with Davido arriving in a horse-drawn carriage, serenading Chioma in grand interiors, and later recreating a proposal scene by a lake at dusk, where he goes down on one knee to present her with a ring.

Though the couple wedded in a lavish Lagos ceremony in June 2024, the proposal scene is a cinematic metaphor for renewed commitment, not a new engagement.

Davido announced the release himself with the caption: “Already Falling. From us to you. Enjoy.”

Like other music stars, Davido is proving that a real-life love story can become a powerful artistic brand.

For fans, ‘Already Falling’ is more than a music video. It is a continuation of a story they have followed since 2018 ; from young lovers, to husband and wife, to parents, told in Davido’s most personal songs. And with Chioma by his side in the studio, on screen, and on tour, including their recent high-profile trip to Tanzania with Diamond Platnumz, the couple shows no signs of slowing down.

World.title: Peter Obi’s Campaign Shuts Down Onitsha in Show of Strength
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

*NDC presidential candidate promises 10,000MW power supply, 50,000 classrooms

David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr. Peter Obi, yesterday shut down the commercial city of Onitsha, Anambra State, as his campaign train moved through the city, attracting massive crowds of supporters.

Obi’s campaign train moved from his residence in the GRA to the First Niger Bridgehead, attracting supporters as it made its way through the streets of Onitsha. The roadshow passed through the First Niger Bridge, Ochanja Market, Main Market, Ose Okwodu Market and several other popular streets in the city, causing heavy traffic congestion and attracting more supporters along the route.



Although his visit slowed commercial activities in the city, many residents gladly joined the campaign train as it passed through their areas. Others reportedly fuelled their vehicles and made them available to convey supporters wearing NDC vests and carrying the party’s flags.

The campaign train berthed at All Saints Anglican Church, where other candidates of the party and their supporters were waiting for his arrival for the proposed town hall meeting.



Meanwhile, the NDC presidential candidate declared January 16, 2027, a public holiday for vote defence. Obi stated this while addressing party supporters at Bishop Patterson Hall, All Saints Anglican Church, Onitsha.

The candidate, while reacting to his supporter’s insistence on singing the old national anthem, said there was no law banning it and that anyone was therefore free to sing it.



He said: “We started this event with the new national anthem and prayers, so after that, anyone who wants to sing whatever song before speaking is free to do so, and there is nothing wrong with it.”

Speaking on what his government would offer Nigerians, Obi said: “Kwankwaso and I have formed a team, and that is the team that will unite Nigeria. We are not going to have a Nigeria where people will come and kidnap our schoolchildren. We will fight corruption. We want to use public money for public good, and from day one, you will feel it and you will know that a new team is in charge.



“We will move Nigeria from consumption to production, and our people will get jobs. We want a country where, if you’re sick, you go to hospital and not church. We will ensure a functional primary healthcare centre in every ward in Nigeria. We will build 50,000 primary school blocks. We will invest in education, healthcare and other sectors you will be proud of.



“Today, Nigeria only generates, transmits and distributes 4,000 megawatts, but Kwankwaso and I will generate 10,000 megawatts of power. Everything we say here, please take note of it because we will do it. We will not give you excuses because we know that the country is already bad, and we will not tell you we didn’t know it was this bad.



“Nigerians have suffered enough, so all of you are contestants in this election through us. Go out there on that day and take it as a day of sacrifice for Nigeria. Carry your food to the polling unit on that day, vote, stay there for counting and transmission, and make sure there is no rigging. That day is now declared a public holiday for vote defence.



“We are prepared. No one will rig this election. We assure you of our commitment. We want to change the ills of this government. Tinubu removed subsidy and said he would not borrow, but today he has borrowed more money than all the other governments put together. That is what we want to change. We want a president who has energy. He is tired, so we have come to beg him to go and rest.”

Earlier, activist Aisha Yesufu sparked controversy when she began her speech by singing the old national anthem. She insisted that she had committed no wrong by singing it, explaining that it was simply a way of calling on Nigerians and other compatriots to arise and defend their country.



She also stated: “We are not lawless; we’re only people who know our rights. There are people who are being killed today, and when we say, ‘Arise, compatriots’, people say we are lawless. We are not lawless. We are saying we believe in Nigeria.

“There is a merger between the North and the East today. For too long, some people have refused to allow that merger to happen. I keep saying this election is not about Peter Obi but about Nigeria, and when I speak, I am saying that we are not allowing anyone to use us.”

Addressing Obi directly, Yesufu said: “I know you (Peter Obi) are law-abiding, but let me tell you, this is not your campaign; this is our campaign, and our children must be freed in this country because no Nigerian is more Nigerian than us. When we sing and they say it is outlawed, then we ask them what part of the law outlawed it.



“From now on, every Monday, we will wear blue to represent NDC, and every Saturday, we will go to every street to rise and fight for Nigeria and speak to Nigerians to join us, because we have the opportunity of a man who wants to work.”

The Senator representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, Victor Umeh, who spoke on behalf of the party’s candidates, likened the roadshow to the triumphant entry of Jesus into Jerusalem.



He said: “My stand is that Mr Peter Obi is the best candidate running for the presidency, and all Nigerians want him to be president. Anambra and the South-east will give all their votes to Obi. In the North, Kwankwaso will win their votes, and we will win from that foundation. Not one vote will be lost in the South-east, and we can assure you we will lose no votes.”

World.title: Makinde Unveils Bold Plan to Give States, Communities Greater Control of Mineral Resources
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

*APM candidate tackles Fashola over Tinubu’s unfulfilled electricity promise

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and Governor of Oyo State, Engr. Seyi Makinde, has unveiled plans to implement true fiscal federalism with resource control as a core element, enabling states and communities to have greater control over solid mineral resources within their territories without undermining national economic stability.

This comes as the campaign council of the APM candidate blasted a former Governor of Lagos State and erstwhile Minister of Power, Works and Housing, Mr. Babatunde Raji Fashola, over his attempt to defend President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s electricity reforms by claiming that the president never promised Nigerians 24-hour electricity.



Under its vision of a “Federation that Works”, the Makinde-Daura RESET NIGERIA Manifesto faulted the current situation where important decisions affecting exploitation of solid mineral resources within states are made principally at the federal level while the states and communities who bear the consequences of exploitation activities have limited influence over decisions that directly affect their areas.

In a statement, Director of Strategic Communications, Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, noted that states and communities bear the brunt of solid mineral exploitation including environmental damage, unsafe storage of hazardous materials, damaged roads, community conflicts and the responsibility for responding to emergencies, yet the federal Government, in some sectors, retains primary control over mineral licensing and other important decisions.



“Despite the consequences they suffer, states and communities do not fully enjoy direct benefits of the exploitation of solid mineral resources within their territories. To RESET this anomaly, the Makinde government will, upon election, initiate a national conversation on restructuring and resource control,” it added.



It further stressed that under the RESET Manifesto, “Nigeria must examine how greater responsibility for natural resources can be transferred to states, how communities that bear the consequences of resource exploitation can receive a fairer share of the benefits, and how such changes can be implemented without undermining national economic stability.”



“The envisaged conversation will not be another open-ended national conference. Within the first year in office, a Federal Responsibility Review will be completed. The review will identify “functions that should remain exclusively federal, functions that require national standard but state delivery, functions that should be principally state or local and functions that require a published intergovernmental agreement”.



“Under the RESET Manifesto, the review will produce specific constitutional amendment, legislation, fiscal changes and transition arrangements. The Makinde RESET Nigeria government will strengthen operation between Federal and State regulatory authorities, established publicly acceptable registers of mining licenses and beneficial ownership, and introduce clearer mechanisms for monitoring compliance while addressing dangerous or illegal mining activities.



“The RESET Agenda proposes a people-oriented situation where “the Federal Government continues to issue mining licenses under the existing constitutional framework, state governments will be formally involved in the licensing process, with opportunities to review applications, raise concerns about land use, environmental xaand public safety.”



This approach provides answers to issues of restrictions, youth restiveness government-community clashes, community-community clashes and indiscriminate exploitation of solid minerals while guaranteeing socio-economic stability, shared prosperity and overall national development.



According to the statement, the Makinde objective was a “federation in which states have greater responsibility for developing their economic potentials, communities benefit more directly from the resources around them and national institutions continue to protect the interest of all Nigerians”.

“The driving ideology of the RESET Nigeria Agenda is the opportunities it creates, the jobs it generates and the improvement it delivers in the lives of Nigerians. Our citizens deserve nothing less,” it added.

Makinde Campaign Blasts Fashola Over Tinubu’s Unfulfilled Electricity Promise

Meanwhile, the Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO), in a statement by Ihediwa, yesterday, in Abuja, declared that Fashola’s denial of the clear promise by the President ‘is not only embarrassing but also shows how low All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders can descend to in the attempt to hoodwink Nigerians”.



The MDPCO noted that since his assumption of office in 2023, President Tinubu’s electricity reforms have “barely moved a needle”.

The President, the APM presidential campaign organisation maintained, has continued on empty boasts of electricity reforms and interventions in infrastructure, metering and market governance. It asked: What has been the result?



According to the statement, under President Tinubu’s ineffective watch Nigeria’s electricity crisis continue to worsen with Nigeria leading in world’s energy deficiency where estimated 86.8 million citizens still not having access to public electricity connection -the highest deficit globally-with no hope in sight given the consistent collapse of the national grid.



The statement read, “In a recent interview on a national TV, former Governor of Lagos State and erstwhile Minister for Power, Works and Housing, Raji Fasola made an attempt to defend President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s electricity reforms by claiming that the president never promised Nigerians 24-hour electricity.



“Fashola’s denial of the clear promise by the President is not only embarrassing but also shows how low All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders can descend to in the attempt to hoodwink Nigerians.

“For the avoidance of doubt, we will reproduce President Tinubu’s exact words:

“Whichever way, by all means necessary, you must have electricity. And you will not pay for estimated bill anymore. A promise made, will be a promise kept.



“If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver.”

A breakdown of President Tinubu’s promise, according to the MDPCO, goes as follows, “You must have electricity” “You will not pay estimated bill anymore”. The question is, Has President Tinubu kept his promises?



“Since his assumption of office in 2023, President Tinubu’s electricity reforms have barely moved a needle. The President continues on empty boasts of electricity reforms and interventions in infrastructure, metering and market governance. What has been the result?

“Under President Tinubu’s ineffective watch Nigeria’s electricity crisis continue to worsen with Nigeria leading in worlds energy deficiency where estimated 86.8 million citizens still not having access to public electricity connection -the highest deficit globally-with no hope in sight given the consistent collapse of the national grid.



“In Fashola’s attempt to defend President Tinubu’s failed assertion that Nigerians ‘will not pay estimated bill anymore’, he claimed that he does not have the numbers.

“Simple research would have shown him that according to the NERC, 4.70 million electricity customers in Nigeria remain without meters and are still exposed to estimated billing. Again, President Tinubu did not keep his promise.



“Fasola was quick to tell Nigerians that the President punctuated his promise with a caveat. So, what are the adequate reasons the administration has given for not keeping its promise.



“Tinubu apologists are always in a hurry to point to infrastructure constraints, legacy debts and the responsibilities of privately operated distribution companies. But these were the same reasons that existed before President Tinubu made the promise.

“President Tinubu has continued reforms, signed laws but we have little evidence that this has impacted availability of electricity for Nigerians.



“Our review of the NERC’s May 2025 Performance Improvement Plan order for the Transmission Company of Nigeria and the Nigerian Independent System Operator shows that only N1.7 billion had been disbursed for eight projects between January 2024 and January 2025.

“It also indicates that only 45% of approved funding for 2024 had reached the dedicated account while identifying other problems such as procurement-clearance delays and inadequate prioritisation as having delayed the project. in fact, the revised core portfolio fell from 142 projects to 50.



“In fact, instead of resolving the issues with the national grid, President Tinubu moved Aso Rock off the national grid and into a solar powered electricity system. We cannot find a better definition for cluelessness and lack of commitment to promise made.

“From all indications, the Tinubu administration is in above its head when it comes to solving electricity problems and no amount of defense for failure by Fashola or any other person for that matter, can turn on a light bulb.



“What is required is action. Nigeria’s problem is not simply generating electricity, or distribution, it requires a value chain approach and this is what the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and its Presidential Candidate, Engr. Seyi Makinde offer with the RESET Nigeria Agenda.

“Engr. Makinde, an Electrical Engineer, has already mapped out strategies to lift Nigeria from the current electricity crisis. In the Reset Nigeria Agenda, the electricity proposition is to improve the reliability and stability of supply within three years by connecting decisions, funding and accountability across the complete delivery chain.



“The Reset Agenda will move from creating new project lists to ensuring that projects are implemented.

“We therefore counsel former minister and other Fashola to stop ridiculing themselves but be courageous enough to accept President Tinubu’s manifest failures.



“Fashola should display statesmanship by supporting Engr. Makinde, whose RESET Agenda offers credible alternative to President Tinubu’s lethargic, clueless and ineffective government”, the statement concluded.

Against this backdrop, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organization urges Nigerians to come out enmasse on January 16, 2027 to vote for APM so that Engr. Makinde can commence the onerous task of Resetting our nation to one that works for all.

World.title: Tinubu Takes Re-election Campaign to South-west
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu will today take his 2027 re-election campaign to his geopolitical zone, the South-west, as he leads chieftains of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to a campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital.

The President, who is scheduled to arrive at Ladoke Akintola Airport in Ibadan by 11 a.m., according to the itinerary sighted by THISDAY yesterday, is expected to meet traditional rulers from across the South-west at the airport before proceeding to Mapo Hall to address party faithful.



The first-class traditional rulers expected to meet with the President include the Ooni of Ife, Olubadan of Ibadanland, Alake of Egbaland, Ewi of Ado Ekiti, Soun of Ogbomoso, Ataoja of Osogbo, Olu of Ilaro and Timi of Ede, among others.

After meeting with the monarchs, Tinubu will proceed to Mapo Hall, where he is expected to inaugurate security vehicles procured by the South-west Development Commission (SWDC) for the region.



The campaign rally, scheduled for 1 p.m., will thereafter commence, with the President leading other APC chieftains, including Vice President Kashim Shettima, 31 state governors, and the National Assembly leadership, represented by Senate President Godswill Akpabio and House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas.

Today’s rally will mark the seventh state Tinubu will be at his re-election campaign rally since the exercise commenced in Kaduna on October 24, 2026.



In the revised campaign timetable released earlier this week by the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Tinubu is scheduled to campaign in 19 of the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The President, who had earlier campaigned in Uyo, Port Harcourt, Dutse, Jos and Birnin Kebbi, is also scheduled to take the campaign train to 13 other cities between November 25, 2026, and January 13, 2027. They are Maiduguri, Enugu, Katsina, Kano, Jalingo, Abuja, Gusau, Owerri, Yola, Sokoto, Ilorin, Asaba and Lagos.

World.title: Atiku Loses Bid to Amend Suit Seeking to Bar Tinubu from 2027 Poll
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Alex Enumah in Abuja

Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has lost in his bid to amend his suit seeking to disqualify President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, from the January 16, 2027 general elections.



This followed the dismissal of his application for amendment by Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court, Abuja, yesterday.

Atiku had approached the court for an order disqualifying Tinubu from participating in next year’s presidential polls, on the grounds that he (Tinubu) forged the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate, submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in aid of his qualification for the presidential election.



However, after President Tinubu, his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the electoral body had responded to the suit, Atiku subsequently applied to amend his originating summons, a request which was opposed by the defendants.

Delivering ruling yesterday, Justice Ekwo declined to grant the request for amendment on the grounds among others that Atiku by the application intended to bring fresh evidence in the suit, which must be done within 14 days stipulated by Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution, being a pre-election matter.



Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and other defendants in the suit that if Atiku is allowed to bring fresh evidence, the character of the initial case would change and would be in breach of the 1999 Constitution.



Ekwo noted that the former vice president by the application attempted to mislead the court when he claimed that he would not present fresh issue in the amendment sought, adding that Atiku through the motion sought to substitute old evidence for a new one which, if allowed, would over reach Section 285(9) of the Constitution which says such evidence must have been provided within 14 days.

According to the judge, a fundamental injustice would be done to the defendants if Atiku is permitted to bring fresh evidence through the back door against them.



“This is a time bound suit and the law makes it mandatory for all exhibits to be filed in court within 14 days of occurrence of the event being challenged. Anything outside the prescribed 14 days is null and void and of no effect.

“I find no merit in this application to bring fresh exhibit, it is hereby refused for being against the express provision of the law.

“I hereby make an order dismissing this application and is hereby dismissed,” Ekwo held.



He subsequently fixed December 2 for hearing of the substantive matter.

Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendment to his case challenging the eligibility of Tinubu to participate in the 2027 presidential election.



Atiku and ADC had in the main suit asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify President Tinubu and APC from the 2027 presidential election.

They had questioned Tinubu’s National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) by APC.



The plaintiffs, who sued the President, APC and INEC as 1st to 3rd defendants in the originating summons marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that APC submitted the President’s forged NYSC discharge certificate to INEC.

They, therefore, prayed the court to compel INEC to remove Tinubu and APC’s names from the list of candidates and parties for the presidential poll.



But President Tinubu and APC, in their joint counter affidavit filed on September 9, prayed the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety for being incompetent and that the plaintiffs lacked the legal right to institute the case.

They denied submitting any forged certificate to INEC either for the 2023 or 2027 presidential elections.

The duo, through the APC’s Director of Legal Services, Mr. Sanusi Samaila, averred that they did not submit any Form CF001 to INEC for 2023 or 2027 poll as claimed by the plaintiffs.

They stated that the NYSC has never denied issuing the discharge certificate to the 1st defendant at the end of his service year.

World.title: Opposition Coalition Moves to Forge United Front, Eyes Consensus Presidential Candidate Nov. 30
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

Opposition political parties under the Coalition for Democracy are intensifying efforts to forge a united front ahead of the 2027 general election, with a consensus presidential candidate expected to emerge from their November 30 summit.

The coalition has shifted its earlier plan to hold the summit on Monday, November 23, 2026, to allow all member parties, presidential candidates and national chairmen to participate fully.

The member parties requested the postponement, citing tight campaign schedules and the need to ensure the participation of their leaders.



The Coalition for Democracy is a multi-party platform pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP).



According to a statement by the National Coordinator of the Coalition for Democracy (formerly G100 Coalition), Mohammed Lukman, the candidates and their campaign teams were now deeply engaged in demanding programmes across the country.

Lukman said the Central Leadership Committee had granted the request and rescheduled the summit to Monday, November 30, 2026.

In the statement, Lukman said, “It is more important that every party, every presidential candidate and every national chairman is in the room than that the Summit holds on its original date,”.



He said that, in consultation with key stakeholders, the committee had agreed on November 30 to secure the widest possible participation.



To demonstrate that commitment, he said all member parties had agreed to suspend campaign activities nationwide on Monday, November 30, to enable their leaders to attend the summit.

Accordingly, “Parties competing hard for votes are prepared to stand down their campaigns for a day, together, because the defence of Nigeria’s democratic space is bigger than any one campaign,” the Coalition for Democracy said.

The summit will finalise and sign the coalition’s common agreement and set the course for its activities ahead of the January 16, 2027 elections.



“We will walk into that room united, and walk out of it committed,” the committee added.

The committee thanked member parties, delegates and partners for their understanding and regretted any inconvenience caused by the change.

It said the venue and accreditation details remained as communicated, adding that any further updates would be shared with delegates and the media in due course.

World.title: ICCEF honours Bestman for Youth Empowerment
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The Innocent Chukwuma Chukwuma Empowerment Foundation has honoured the founder of Talent Spotlight Africa Foundation, Lilian Amaka Bestman, with the 2026 Innocent Chukwuma Award for Social Innovation in Southeast Nigeria.

Bestman, an educationist, entrepreneur and business coach, received the award at the Social Innovators Programme and Awards 2026 organised by LEAP Africa, alongside a cash prize of N300,000.

According to a statement by ICEEF’s communications specialist, Ohunene Majebi, yesterday, the recognition was for her contributions to youth empowerment, entrepreneurship education and economic inclusion through Talent Spotlight Africa Foundation, which operates mainly in Rivers and Enugu states.

Through the foundation, Bestman has promoted entrepreneurship education, practical skills development, leadership training and mentorship for young people and women.

According to the foundation, more than 20,000 young adults and women have benefited from its entrepreneurship education, skills training and capacity-building programmes.

One of its recent initiatives, the Inter-Secondary School Entrepreneurship Competition, brought together more than 300 students from public secondary schools in Rivers State in 2026, challenging them to develop entrepreneurial ideas and solutions to real-life problems.

The foundation has also distributed more than 5,000 learning materials to secondary schools in three local government areas of Rivers State and donated over 2,000 copies of Bestman’s book, Nine Lights to Success, to schools in Rivers and Enugu states.

Beyond the statistics, Bestman said the foundation had witnessed individual beneficiaries turn acquired skills into sources of livelihood.

She recalled the case of a participant who developed an interest in cosmetology after taking part in one of the foundation’s entrepreneurship programmes and eventually began earning an income that helped her finance her tertiary education.

The award is part of ICCEF’s Legacy Programme, established to preserve and advance the values of the late Innocent Chukwuma, a human rights advocate and social justice campaigner who championed institutional reform, social change and the empowerment of underserved communities.

Through the award, the foundation recognises individuals developing innovative solutions to social challenges and contributing to positive change in Southeast Nigeria.

Reacting to the recognition, Bestman described it as a significant milestone for herself and Talent Spotlight Africa Foundation.

She said, “It is not a destination, but motivation to do more and transform more lives.”

Bestman said the recognition would further strengthen the foundation’s resolve to expand its programmes, deepen partnerships and reach more underserved communities.

She added that TSA planned to scale up its entrepreneurship education and practical skills initiatives while expanding mentorship opportunities for young people seeking sustainable livelihoods.

The foundation said Bestman’s recognition underscored the importance of grassroots innovation and practical education in tackling youth unemployment, economic exclusion and limited access to opportunities.

World.title: Abians Optimistic As First US-Africa Trade Confab Ends in Umuahia
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Many Abians have expressed optimism that the US-Africa Trade and Investment Conference and Expo (AfrICANDO 2026), which ended in Umuahia on Thursday, would achieve its goal of connecting businesses in the state with the world.

The conference, which began on Tuesday, brought together businesses, international investors, development institutions, technical partners and global markets from Africa, Europe and the United States of America.

On display at the International Conference Centre, Umuahia, venue of the three-day conference, were various locally-made products, including agricultural produce, footwears, Akwete local fabrics, among others.

The Chief of Staff to the Governor, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, who also served as the Chairman of the Local Organising Committee (LOC), described the conference as a strategic platform for unlocking Africa’s economic potential, noting that Abia State was the first to host the conference in Africa.

“Bringing the conference to Umuahia presented Abia with an opportunity to showcase its economic potential, strengthen international business relationships and create pathways for local enterprises to participate more effectively in global commerce,” Ajagba said.

According to him, Abia was already looking beyond the successful hosting to reaping the accrued benefits of the 27th business conference, which, he said, reflected Governor Alex Otti’s determination to reposition the state as a competitive destination for global investment and business partnerships, with the prospect of attracting foreign capital and accelerating industrial development.

He added that the conference aligned with the administration’s broader economic vision of building a productive economy driven by private-sector investment, industrialisation, enterprise development and employment generation. He explained that the state was particularly interested in translating the international exposure generated by AfrICANDO into concrete investment commitments, commercial partnerships and sustainable economic benefits for its people.

Commenting on the conference, the Chief Executive Officer of the Abia State Diaspora Commission, Ambassador Annie Onu, said it could reposition Abia, particularly Aba, as a major manufacturing and export hub through the opportunity to connect local businesses with global investors and development partners.

She said the state was ready for international business partnerships in manufacturing, agriculture, real estate and cultural enterprises.

Governor Otti, while declaring the event open, had wooed investors to the state while advocating a new paradigm in economic relations between the United States and Africa, anchored on trade, investment and economic integration rather than aid, to usher in prosperity and end poverty, destitution and exploitation on the continent, a new vista AFRICANDO has opened.

He said the state is specifically targeting investments in manufacturing, real estate, hospitality, agricultural value chains, ICT and others, because the atmosphere in Abia is very conducive and supportive of those ventures.

The governor said that over the last three years, his administration has, through deliberate and strategic investments in public infrastructure, security and social services, repositioned the state, particularly Aba, the commercial nerve centre of the region, into a favourite investment destination. He said priority was given to the restoration and expansion of Aba’s infrastructure because of the city’s historical eminence as a prime industrial and commercial centre.

On exploring a new roadmap for US-Africa relationship, Otti noted that Africa’s paradox of poverty amidst abundance of prized natural resources had dominated global economic conversations for five decades, yet aid had failed to address the fundamental issues of low productivity and restricted access to global markets.

He noted that governments and institutions in the United States and across Western Europe had committed an estimated $2 trillion in overseas development assistance to Africa since the 1970s, but the continent still accounts for more than 70 per cent of global extreme poverty.

“If the continent’s poverty crisis still persists, after over five decades of aids and trillions of dollars in humanitarian interventions, the next course of action would be to acknowledge that Africa needs a new development paradigm to defeat poverty,” he said.

He said the post-aid relationship, anchored by economic cooperation and fair access to markets and resources, will open Africa to a new era of prosperity when the technological and industrial leadership of the West is matched with the continent’s abundant natural and human resources.

Otti said AFRICANDO draws from the optimism of that emerging paradigm, founded on individual and collective responsibility, and a shift from dependence to interdependence, even as Africa looks to developed economies for market access and institutional support.

He thanked the Foundation for Democracy in Africa (FDA) and the Abia Global Chamber of Commerce for bringing the first AFRICANDO event to be hosted on the continent to Abia, describing it as a big boost to artisans, small business owners, industrialists, investors and multilateral partners.

World.title: REC Appeals for Participation as INEC Holds Mock Voter Accreditation in 598 Delta’s Polling Units
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Delta State, Sir Etekamba Udo Umoren, has appealed to citizens and the electorate in the state to actively participate in the commission’s mock Bimodal Voter Accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, 2026.

Umoren said that the test of Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC’s) Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and result upload processes would be conducted in 598 polling units selected across the 25 local government areas of the state on November 28 to enable INEC identify areas of possible technical challenges as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections.

Briefing journalists yesterday in Asaba, the Delta REC assured that the exercise would enable the Commission determine the configuration accuracy of the electoral equipment and systems preparatorily to the 2027 election, noting the selection of the units was to ensure good geographical scope.

The REC said, “The Mock Accreditation and Result Upload will be conducted across the 25 local government areas of Delta State on 28th November, 2026. The polling units will open by 7.30amand Accreditation will commence at 8am and close at 2 30pm.

“The commission is using 598 Polling Units across the 25 LGAs, two units per Registration Area (ward) in Delta State will be selected and utilised for the exercise.

“We have 25 local government areas in the state and 299 registration areas, otherwise called wards. If you multiply 299 by two, it gives you 598 polling units. That is how we arrived at the 598 polling units.

“The exercise will provide an opportunity to test the functionality and reliability of technologies and equipment, particularly the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS).

“It will also access the effectiveness of the accreditation, voting, result recording, transmission, and other relevant Election-Day processes, as applicable to the exercise.”

Moreover, the Mock Accreditation and Result Upload exercise would help INEC determine the preparedness of its personnel, including the “neutrality” of its regular and ad-hoc staff, in terms of understanding of polling procedures, proper handling of election materials, accreditation, voting, sorting, counting as well as result management, he stressed.

On logistical arrangements, Umoren said that the exercise will also test the commission’s preparedness for “timely deployment of personnel, election materials, equipment and other resources to designated polling units.”

He also responded to questions on INEC’s real time electronic transmission of election results from polling units to the INEC Result Viewing Portal and the commission’s preparedness to ensure hitch-free upload of polling results that accurately reflected the action of the electorate in the election proper.

Umoren said, “It is for us to look at whether we have properly set or configured the system to work the way they should. If there is any technical issue, that will be corrected.

“These are the likely situations we want to identify. The exercise will give us a clear picture, and then we will know whether we have properly configured the system and whether it is ready for the election.”

“It is important to emphasise that the mock accreditation is not the actual election and will not involve the declaration of winners and losers,” noted the Delta State REC, who was flanked by the Administrative Secretary, Davis O. Eldred, and other management staff the commission in the state.

Umoren also appealed to stakeholders, including registered political parties, security agencies, civil society organisations as well as community leaders and the media to collaborate with the INEC to ensure that eligible voters participate and that the exercise is peaceful and successful.

World.title: SASSA grants suspended over one-time deposit: Is that FAIR?
World.content:
SASSA grants are being suspended over the smallest one-time cash deposits. Surely, that's not fair? Image: File

Two beneficiaries report their SASSA grants suspended after a review was triggered. Here’s what these two unfortunate individuals went through, so you don’t have to.

The first is a Chatsworth woman (64), who didn’t want to be named. Her case was reported back in July. A single R500 deposit from a family member was the trigger. Next, a Merebank man (65) received R2 000 from his child …

SASSA GRANTS SUSPENDED
