World.title: Analyst: Center Party support rose off back of anti-corruption committee work
World.content:
The Riigikogu's Anti-Corruption Select Committee has helped boost support for the opposition Center Party, according to one pollster.

The Riigikogu's Anti-Corruption Select Committee's investigation into defense scandals helped lift support for the Center Party, Kantar Emor polling expert Aivar Voog said. Center Party MP Anastassia Kovalenko-Kõlvart chairs the committee.

The Center Party took the outright lead in Emor's November party rankings, commissioned by the ERR newsroom, with 24.7 percent support, up from 20.6 percent a month earlier. Two more opposition parties, the Social Democrats (SDE) and Isamaa follow in second and third, polling at 20.5 percent and 18.9 percent, respectively.

The fourth opposition party, the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) remains in fourth place with 13.8 percent support, virtually unchanged from the previous month.

Support for the senior coalition partner, the Reform Party, and the non-parliamentary Parempoolsed fell in November. The fifth-placed Reform Party's rating dropped from 14.2 percent in October to 10.9 percent, while sixth-placed Parempoolsed fell from 6.5 percent to 5.5 percent.

"Support for the Center Party has now risen for two months in a row, so there's once again a clear leader in the party rankings. Last month, three parties were at roughly the same level. Now the Center Party has pulled ahead," Voog said, speaking to ERR's ratings special broadcast, hosted by Aleksander Krjukov and Johannes Voltri.

"If you look at the changes across demographic groups, the shift was mainly among women, where support rose from 21 percent to 29 percent. Among men voters, it stayed at roughly the same level," Voog went on.

Voog said that since the defense scandals broke which cost Reform Party Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur his job at the start of September, the Center Party has been able to criticize the government and keep itself in the public eye through hearings held by the Riigikogu's Anti-Corruption Select Committee, chaired by Kovalenko-Kõlvart.

Voog said Center and SDE had taken over from Isamaa as the government's main critics, leaving Isamaa somewhat in the background.

Voltri noted Center's support was last this high in March 2019, the month prior to the party entering office with Isamaa and EKRE. He added that there was, however, considerable uncertainty around its polling numbers, and that support could drop quite suddenly.

Krjukov added that one risk facing the Center Party was that voters who speak Russian at home, a traditional support bedrock for the party, might stay away from the polls on election day. Voog agreed that this had happened in the past, including at the last two Riigikogu elections.

"That was the case in 2019 and especially in 2023, when turnout among voters of other ethnicities was significantly lower than among ethnic Estonian voters. That led to a historically low result for the Center Party in 2023," Voog said.

Aivar Voog, Aleksander Krjukov andJohannes Voltri on Friday's election special. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"If you look at how sure voters are of their choice, you can see that the party has picked up more voters whose preference is less firmly held," the analyst added.

Voog said Isamaa, but not EKRE, has been facing the same problem. "Isamaa was in the lead, but many of its supporters weren't firmly committed to the party. And that's what sets all three of the current frontrunners — the Center Party, the Social Democrats and Isamaa — apart from EKRE, for example. They have far more voters whose preferences could easily change. There's no guarantee that support will hold, and the balance between the parties could still shift significantly before the election," he said.

Voog said former Foreign Ministry Secretary General Jonatan Vseviov's decision throw his hat into the ring and run for SDE, and his confirmation as their prime ministerial candidate too, had helped keep the party's support above the 20-percent level.

"That helped stabilize their support. In the past, when the Social Democrats saw a sharp rise one month, their rating typically fell by just as much the next," Voog explained.

Voog noted that Isamaa had been getting less attention since slipping to third place, though it has more money to spend on advertising than Center and so could use that to raise its profile between now and the March 2027 election.

Voog said past experience has demonstrated that a sense of novelty could sustain a party's rating for about six months, which also helped explain the decline in Isamaa's support.

"They started rising just after the 2023 Riigikogu elections and stayed near their peak for almost three years. That's a very long time for a party. Eventually people get a little tired of it, and the party no longer seems as fresh," Voog said, adding that Isamaa could counter that by bringing in new members.

Isamaa has lost voters to both SDE and Center, Voog noted.

He explained that once a party reaches a rating of about 20 percent, its voter base becomes more diverse. "Core supporters make up a smaller share, and you also have voters who simply go with whoever is more popular, more fashionable or seems fresher at the time," he said.

Voog said the Reform Party was still in a strong position at the end of the summer, but that the situation had deteriorated for them through the fall. "The economy was looking better. Prices were rising more slowly, inflation was somewhere around 2 percent and consumer confidence was growing. Now prices have started rising again as global oil prices have gone up. Utility costs and electricity prices have also risen. The jump was already visible in October's power market prices, and now it's showing up in household bills, which are nearly 50 percent higher. Those conditions make it harder for the Reform Party to maintain that level of support," Voog said.

Voog said the Reform Party would get a clear boost in the polls if former Estonian Defense Forces commander Martin Herem were to announce he would run for the party at the Riigikogu elections after all. "Whether Martin Herem runs on their ticket is a very important question for the Reform Party," he said.

Herem replaced Pevkur as defense minister but has not announced any intention to run.

World.title: Three Estonian theaters win three-year state funding
World.content:
Tartu New Theater, VAT Theater and Von Krahl Theater have secured three-year operating grants as the Culture Ministry distributes €3 million in funding among private theaters.

The ministry's funding round will see eight private theaters share the €3 million, while Tallinn City Theater, the only municipal applicant, will receive a separate €900,000.

Funding applications totaled nearly €7.8 million.

The three highest-scoring applicants — Tartu New Theater, VAT Theatre and Von Krahl Theater — were recommended for three-year grants. Five theaters have previously received funding on the same three-year basis: Tartu New Theater, Von Krahl Theater, Kanuti Gildi SAAL, Theater R.A.A.A.M. and the Expedition.

This year's applications were assessed using a revised methodology developed with performing arts representatives and designed to address shortcomings in the funding system. It adjusts the weighting of evaluation criteria as well as the formula used to calculate grants.

The changes also exclude individual scores that deviate significantly from the assessment committee's average.

"This makes the assessment result less susceptible to exceptionally high or low scores from one or two committee members and better reflects the committee's overall view," explained ministry theater adviser and committee chair Marie Anett Heinsalu.

The committee assessed artistic quality, creative plans, diversity of programming, regional activity and budget feasibility. Applicants needed at least 75 points out of 100 to qualify, with their scores determining the share of the requested amount they received.

Top theaters praised for ambition, engagement and improving quality

Tartu New Theater scored the highest with 88 points and will receive €543,726, against a request of €750,000.

The assessment committee praised the theater's artistic ambition, willingness to take creative risks and ability to combine research with compelling theatrical form, despite acknowledging that not all its risk-taking projects have been equally successful.

VAT Theater received 87 points and €521,887 in funding, after likewise requesting €750,000.

The committee highlighted its established artistic profile, work for young audiences and engagement with socially relevant issues, noting that the theater's use of guest artists and experimental productions had led to some variation in quality, but also allowed it to explore new forms.

Von Krahl Theater scored 83 points and will receive €467,857, against a request of €750,000.

The assessment committee said that with a new ensemble, the theater's artistic quality had improved and its identity grown more distinctive in recent years. While the committee noted some unevenness, it also noted that the theater's repertoire combines acclaimed productions and professional execution with experimentation.

Five other private theaters that scored between 75 and 79 points will also receive grants, including €209,570 for the Estonian Dance Agency, €362,934 for Vaba Lava, €237,252 for the Independent Dance Stage (STL), €350,935 for Kanuti Gildi SAAL and €305,839 for the Expedition.

Tallinn City Theater, the only municipal theater to apply, also scored 75 points and will receive €900,000, below the €1.15 million it requested.

The assessment committee praised the theater's experienced ensemble and strong production and organizational expertise, but said its artistic output had been uneven, with room to strengthen its artistic ambition and create a more cohesive repertoire. It also noted limited artistic renewal and engagement with contemporary social issues.

Two theaters miss out

Two applicants, Theatrum and Impro Theater IMPEERIUM, missed out on funding after scoring below the required 75-point threshold.

Theatrum, which requested €714,262, scored just 65 points. The committee praised the theater's established focus on classical drama, philosophy and literature, but found its recent output uneven and its creative circle narrow, with little renewal in its repertoire or staging.

Impro Theater IMPEERIUM, meanwhile, scored 61 points after requesting €300,044. While the committee recognized its established position in improvisational theater, it said the company's artistic ambition and execution remained limited by wider professional theater standards, citing room for improvement in dramatic structure, performers' skills and moving beyond recurring improvisational techniques.

Smaller Estonian theaters, meanwhile, will have another option this year: for the first time, they can apply for one-year operating grants from the Cultural Endowment of Estonia. About €650,000 a year is earmarked for the scheme, on top of existing funding for the theater sector.

The assessment committee included representatives appointed by performing arts organizations and the Ministry of Culture.

World.title: Defense Forces issue, lift drone threat warning for northeast Estonia
World.content:
The Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) issued, and later lifted, a potential drone threat warning for Lääne-Viru and Ida-Viru counties early Saturday.

The alert went out at 4:42 a.m. via Estonia's public warning system, EE-ALARM.

In a comment to ERR, the EDF confirmed that NATO fighter jets — specifically Turkish Air Force aircraft — were airborne in response.

An ERR reader reported hearing a drone over Väike-Maarja in Lääne-Viru County at 6:13 a.m., followed roughly a minute later by the sound of a fighter jet.Unlike in earlier incidents, where public broadcasters in Latvia and Lithuania reported airspace alerts before drones reached Estonia, neither country issued such warnings early Saturday.

At 6:49 a.m., the EDF announced that the aerial threat in Lääne-Viru and Ida-Viru counties had passed.

Meanwhile, Alexander Drozdenko, governor of Russia's neighboring Leningrad Oblast, said via Russian state news agency Interfax early Saturday that air defenses had downed six drones."Six enemy unmanned aerial vehicles were shot down over the Leningrad region. Combat operations are ongoing," Drozdenko wrote on the messaging app Max. Less than an hour later, he stated that the number of downed drones had risen to 93.

Finland restricts air, sea traffic in eastern Gulf of Finland

The Finnish Defense Forces also imposed temporary restrictions on maritime areas and airspace in the eastern Gulf of Finland early Saturday.

In a post on social media platform X, the Finnish military said the restrictions were a precautionary measure aimed at ensuring the safety of bystanders and maintaining operational freedom for the authorities.

These authorities were preparing to counter potential drones in the area, with the temporary restrictions taking effect shortly after 4 a.m. Finland last imposed similar restrictions just over a week ago.

Due to Russia's war against Ukraine, aerial vehicles, including drones, may inadvertently enter Estonian airspace or be directed toward it by Russia.

The EDF uses EE-ALARM channels to notify the public both of potential aerial threats and when residents are required to take shelter.

The EDF most recently issued similar EE-ALARM air threat warnings across eight southern and eastern counties, including Lääne-Viru and Ida-Viru, early on November 11. The alerts prompted NATO fighter jets to scramble as Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Ust-Luga port in Leningrad Oblast, 36 kilometers from the Estonian border.

Editor's note: This piece was updated to include information about Finland's airspace and maritime restrictions.

World.title: Estonia's Foreign Ministry summons Russian chargé d'affaires
World.content:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) has summoned Russia's chargé d'affaires over recent attacks on Kyiv and to announce Estonia's decision to close its eastern border.

The Russian diplomat was summoned by the ministry Friday to protest Russia's large-scale missile and drone attacks on Kyiv in recent days. Thursday's strikes damaged several European diplomatic missions, including the Austrian and Dutch embassies.

The Foreign Ministry also informed the chargé d'affaires that Estonia will be closing all road border checkpoints along its border with Russia from December 1 in response to what it called Russia's hostile activities.

"Putin continues to systematically attack Ukrainian cities, infrastructure and people," Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said, adding that Russian strikes are targeting energy, economic and transport infrastructure as well as hospitals, schools, cafes and cultural institutions.

He noted that nearly 700 civilians have been killed or injured in the past week alone.

"Until Russia ends its aggression and takes responsibility for its actions, our efforts must focus on two objectives: increasing pressure on Russia and providing comprehensive support to Ukraine," Tsahkna said.

'It's our duty to protect Estonia and the EU border'

He described the Estonian government's Friday decision to close the road border with Russia for at least the next six months as an important security measure, saying the move would limit opportunities for Russia to recruit people, conduct influence operations, organize sabotage and evade sanctions through cross-border movement.

"It is our duty to protect Estonia's security and the European Union's external border," the minister stressed, adding that Estonia also must not allow Russia to sow fear and uncertainty or divert attention away from supporting Ukraine.

World.title: Estonian racing driver Paul Aron leaves Alpine Formula One team
World.content:
Estonian racing driver Paul Aron has parted ways with Formula One team Alpine by mutual agreement after two seasons as a reserve driver, to pursue a full-time race seat.

According to motorsport outlet Gpblog, starting a third season as a reserve at the U.K.-based outfit held little appeal for the 22-year-old, as he wants to return to full-time racing.

"BWT Alpine Formula One Team and Paul Aron have mutually agreed to release Paul from his role as reserve driver and his other obligations within the team, in order to allow him to pursue other opportunities in motorsport." the team said in a statement released on Friday.

"The team extends its sincere thanks to Paul for his work as a reserve driver over the past two seasons and wishes him all the best for the future.," the statement went on.

With Argentine driver Franco Colapinto and France's Pierre Gasly locked in as Alpine's main race drivers for next season, no full-time race seat was open for Aron at the team, which traces its lineage back to the Toleman, later Benetton, team of the 1980s.

Over the past two years, Aron, 22, has taken part in several Grands Prix, but only at free practice sessions, with Alpine and also with Sauber and Audi.

International motorsport media report that Aron could move to the all-electric Formula E series, where several teams are reportedly interested in signing him.

Earlier this week, Aron tested a Formula E car for Fortescue Zero Racing at the Jarama circtui in Spain. While he was involved in a crash there, he was unhurt.

Two years ago, he competed in the Berlin ePrix for Envision Racing, finishing 13th and 14th.

Formula E is the electric cars counterpart to Formula One.

World.title: Ukrainian defense firms showcase latest battlefield tech in Tallinn
World.content:
Ukrainian defense companies are in Tallinn, showcasing their latest battlefield technology at Open Arms Fest as they seek European partners to expand production.

The two-day Tallinn leg of the Open Arms Fest, organized by the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry and its embassy in Tallinn, is being held at the Port of Tallinn Cruise Terminal, where defense company FirePoint stole the spotlight Thursday with a particular replica missile.

The company's technology recently helped bring down part of the Kerch Bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea, as seen in footage that has since gone viral.

The attack also highlighted Ukraine's use of mesh modems carried by relay drones to maintain communications and control links without ground-based infrastructure or SpaceX's Starshield. Russia has used the same system to attack Ukrainian infrastructure.

"I can't say exactly how long it took the adversary, but our network's capabilities were already developed a year ago," said Ukrainian Capt. Valerii Churkin. "They've just started deploying them more widely now."

Open Arms Fest kicked off in Oslo late last month, followed by two-day events in Stockholm and Helsinki before making its way to Tallinn. Ukraine is looking to move some production to Europe, as manufacturing at home remains vulnerable to Russian attacks.

"Localizing production in Ukraine isn't safe," explained festival project manager Kateryna Soliar, adding that moving production to Europe also makes economic sense. "Europeans, in turn, are interested in drawing on Ukrainians' recent battlefield experience."

Ukraine has what Europe lacks

Churkin, a former deputy defense minister tasked with introducing modern warfare methods in Ukraine, now works on similar issues within one of its military units. He said Ukraine's advantage lies in its ability to rapidly develop and refine technology based on battlefield feedback.

"What Ukraine has and Europe lacks is a fast development cycle and rapid feedback on technologies," he said. "Things can change completely in six months — or even just a few weeks in some fields, like electronic warfare."

This summer, Estonia and Ukraine signed a framework agreement on drone cooperation at the NATO summit in Ankara, with Estonia providing investment while Ukraine contributes technology.

World.title: Egypt is working to hold Hamas to its commitments on confining weapons: foreign minister
World.content:
Egyptian Foreign Minister Dr. Badr Abdelatty stressed, in exclusive statements to Asharq Al-Awsat, that Cairo is pressing ahead with efforts to push Palestinian factions, foremost among them Hamas, toward implementing understandings on confining and handing over weapons.

He stressed that transitioning to the second phase of US President Donald Trump's plan to end the war in Gaza requires all parties to honor their commitments, primarily completing the Israeli withdrawal and ensuring the flow of humanitarian aid.

Speaking on the sidelines of his visit to Washington and meetings with senior US lawmakers, Abdelatty said: "The Egyptian side has put forward numerous ideas, and significant efforts are underway regarding the implementation of Palestinian factions' commitments, including Hamas, to confine and surrender weapons."

He added that this step represents vital progress in resolving one of the most complex issues in the arrangements for the next phase of Trump's Gaza plan.

He dismissed suggestions of any maneuvering by Palestinian factions regarding their pledge to hand over weapons.

"We are focusing on what was previously agreed upon in the Cairo meetings, and Hamas leaders have stated they favor confining and handing over weapons," he said, hoping for a "positive response from the Israeli government."

Abdelatty’s remarks underscore Egypt's stance and its push to translate broad political understandings into actionable commitments, particularly on the weapons file, which remains one of the thorniest obstacles to post-war governance and security arrangements in Gaza.

Moving forward requires a clear timeline for handing over the arms and an agreed-upon mechanism to oversee the process, while Israel’s position remains a decisive factor in determining whether these pledges become concrete steps on the ground.

Displacement is a ‘red line’

Abdelatty stressed that Egyptian efforts to implement Trump's plan do not signal any shift in Cairo's core principles regarding the Palestinian cause.

Egypt remains steadfast in supporting the Palestinians' right to self-determination and an independent state with East Jerusalem as its capital, rejecting any attempts to force them off their land, he added.

"Egypt’s positions are well-known and unwavering: full support for the Palestinian people until they secure all their legitimate rights, including self-determination and the establishment of an independent state with East Jerusalem as its capital," he told Asharq Al-Awsat.

"This is our stance and we will not deviate from it. Palestinians have the right to remain on their land; we will not accept displacement, as this is a red line for Egyptian foreign policy."

These assurances reflect Cairo's determination to separate security arrangements concerning factional weapons from the broader political track, which it insists must culminate in an independent Palestinian state.

Egypt is also working to ensure that talks over security arrangements do not become a substitute for addressing political and humanitarian priorities, chiefly future governance in Gaza, reconstruction, and the residents' right to stay on their land.

Outreach in Congress

Abdelatty’s remarks came during a visit to the US capital featuring a series of meetings with Republican and Democratic congressional leaders, aimed at strengthening Cairo's partnership with Washington and rallying support for implementing the second phase of Trump's Gaza plan. Discussions also tackled regional crises spanning Iran, Sudan, and the Red Sea.

During a meeting with US House Speaker Mike Johnson, he underscored the importance of strategic ties between Cairo and Washington and Congress's role in backing bilateral cooperation.

He stressed the need to complete the Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and ensure humanitarian aid delivery, while also supporting diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis with Iran and safeguarding freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

Abdelatty also met with Republican Senator Jim Risch, Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, reviewing Egyptian efforts to de-escalate regional tensions, developments in Gaza and the West Bank, and the Iranian crisis, as well as avenues to boost bilateral economic, trade, and investment cooperation.

In a post-meeting statement, Risch affirmed the importance of the partnership with Egypt in addressing regional crises, pointing specifically to the ongoing conflict in Sudan, working toward lasting peace in the Middle East, and strengthening bilateral ties.

Abdelatty held talks with Rep. Gregory Meeks, the ranking Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Democratic Senator Jeff Merkley, and Democratic Rep. Brad Schneider. Their discussions centered on developments in the Middle East and the Horn of Africa, boosting political and economic cooperation, and preventing regional confrontations from widening.

Coordination regarding the Muslim Brotherhood

Separately, Abdelatty revealed to Asharq Al-Awsat that Egypt is coordinating with the US and European countries on designating the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist organization, stressing that Cairo's position rests on national judicial rulings that it is moving forward to enforce.

"This is a principled stance; rulings have been issued by the Egyptian judiciary - known for its independence and integrity - and these rulings designating the group as terrorist will be enforced," he said.

"These are decisions made at the national level, and there is certainly coordination between Egypt and countries worldwide, particularly Europe and the United States, to reinforce this designation."

Abdelatty’s comments carry weight given shifts in US policy toward the Muslim Brotherhood over the past year and moves within the Trump administration to expand legal and financial measures against the group's branches and affiliated networks.

The FM did not disclose details regarding the coordination mechanisms or the specific European countries involved, nor did he clarify whether consultations focus on intelligence sharing, tracking funding networks, or pushing for further legal designations.

This article was first published on Asharq al-Awsat.

World.title: Saudi telecom operators look beyond data revenue as 5G advances: Ericsson
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s expanding 5G infrastructure is creating opportunities for telecom operators to generate revenue from services beyond conventional mobile data, as advanced network capabilities open new markets among consumers and businesses, according to Ericsson.

Strong adoption, continued network expansion and growing use of fixed wireless access are providing a foundation for operators to offer more specialised connectivity services, Ante Mihovilovic, vice president and head of networks at Ericsson Europe, Middle East and Africa, told Arab News in an interview.

“Saudi Arabia is an important 5G market, supported by strong adoption, continued network expansion and growing use of Fixed Wireless Access,” Mihovilovic said.

He explained that the Kingdom’s progress reflects sustained investment in network capacity, coverage and digital infrastructure rather than a single measure of revenue growth.

The Ericsson official's comments come as Saudi Arabia accelerates telecommunications investment under Vision 2030, with operators expanding network capacity and exploring new services for consumers and businesses.

New revenue streams

Mihovilovic said future growth opportunities would increasingly extend beyond conventional mobile broadband and fixed wireless access to services tailored to specific customer needs.

These include applications in gaming, media, logistics and industrial operations, where network performance and reliability can be particularly important.

Ante Mihovilovic, vice president and head of networks at Ericsson Europe, Middle East and Africa

“The opportunity is to move from selling connectivity mainly by data volume toward services built around performance, reliability and specific network capabilities,” Mihovilovic said.

He identified 5G Standalone, which operates independently of earlier mobile network infrastructure, and network application programming interfaces, or APIs, as technologies that could support this transition.

However, Mihovilovic acknowledged that expanding 5G networks has not always translated into additional revenue for telecom operators.

“One lesson from the global 5G journey is that faster connectivity alone does not automatically create new revenue streams,” he said.

He explained that generating returns from advanced networks depends on developing services customers value and are willing to pay for, alongside suitable business models and partnerships.

AI in networks

Artificial intelligence is also becoming an important tool for improving network efficiency, with operators using the technology to automate processes, optimize performance and manage resources.

“A strong example is Hajj, where AI-driven capabilities help operators manage unprecedented levels of connectivity demand, ensuring reliable network performance and a seamless experience for millions of pilgrims,” he said.

Beyond network management, he noted that growing demand for AI-enabled services and data-intensive applications is increasing the need for reliable, high-performing telecommunications infrastructure.

Smarter networks can support new digital services, while the adoption of those services creates additional demand for network capacity, he explained.

The developments come amid continued investment in Saudi Arabia’s digital infrastructure.

In September, Ericsson and Saudi telecom operator stc group announced a multi-year agreement to expand 5G coverage and capacity across the Kingdom.

The agreement includes deploying additional network sites, expanding 5G Standalone technology and preparing for differentiated connectivity services.

Separately, the Communications, Space and Technology Commission announced more than SR550 million ($146.7 million) in information and communications technology infrastructure investments during LEAP 2026, alongside initiatives to advance 5G technology and network sustainability.

Vision 2030 impact

Mihovilovic said Saudi Arabia’s economic diversification strategy has helped accelerate digital investment, although telecommunications demand is not limited to major developments such as Neom.

“Vision 2030 has created strong momentum for digital investment, but the growth extends beyond individual giga-projects,” he said.

He explained that consumers, businesses and government entities are increasingly requiring more advanced connectivity as services become digital and industries adopt new technologies.

While Vision 2030 has placed digital infrastructure and innovation among the Kingdom’s development priorities, operators are also responding to demand for greater capacity, wider coverage and enterprise services.

Saudi Arabia is seeking to attract further international investment in advanced telecommunications infrastructure.

In April, Communications and Information Technology Minister Abdullah Al-Swaha met Ericsson CEO Borje Ekholm to discuss expanding the company’s investments in advanced 5G networks, cloud infrastructure, AI and automation.

Saudi Minister of Communications and Information Technology Abdullah Alswaha, fourth from right, met President and CEO of Ericsson Borje Ekholm in April. SPA

Ericsson has had a presence in Saudi Arabia for nearly five decades, with Mihovilovic noting that the Kingdom has consistently adopted successive generations of mobile technology.

GCC outlook

The shift toward advanced 5G services is also taking place across the Gulf Cooperation Council, although Mihovilovic said individual markets are likely to pursue different approaches.

Operators across the region are investing in fixed wireless access, 5G Standalone and programmable networks that can provide different levels of performance depending on customer requirements.

“There will not be one identical model across the GCC,” he said.

He explained that Saudi Arabia’s market scale and Vision 2030 priorities create specific opportunities, while other Gulf economies may focus more heavily on smart cities, tourism or enterprise services.

Technologies such as network slicing, which allows operators to allocate network resources to particular applications, and network APIs could be deployed according to each market’s needs.

Growth by 2027

Looking ahead, Mihovilovic identified 5G Standalone and differentiated connectivity as among the strongest potential revenue opportunities for regional telecom operators by 2027.

These technologies could allow operators to offer services based on specific performance and reliability requirements rather than treating connectivity as a standardized product.

“Network APIs can extend this opportunity by giving developers and enterprises access to capabilities such as quality on demand, location and authentication,” he said.

He added that fixed wireless access would remain important as operators seek to generate greater value from their existing network investments.

Mihovilovic emphasized that technology alone would not determine commercial success.

“The industry has learned that monetization depends on turning network capabilities into services that customers clearly value and are willing to pay for,” he said. “Technology is only one part of the equation; operators also need the right service models, partnerships and go-to-market strategies.”

World.title: Iraq fire at Basra power station kills at least four, injures 30
World.content:
BASRA: ‌At least 4 people were killed and 30 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.

Civil defense teams brought the fire at the Hartha ‌power station north ‌of Basra under ‌control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq’s state news agency, INA, reported.

The fire spread to neighboring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said. The Hartha station ‌has ‌an installed generating capacity of 800 megawatts ‌but had been operating ‌at around 400 megawatts before the fire, they said.

There was no immediate official information on the ‌cause of the fire or the extent of the damage, INA reported.

Iraq’s electricity infrastructure has long struggled with decades of underinvestment, inadequate maintenance and an inability to meet peak demand, particularly during the extremely hot summer months. Fires and technical failures at substations and power facilities have previously disrupted electricity supplies and caused widespread outages.

World.title: Israeli settlers’ move into a Palestinian neighborhood brings deadly violence to Jericho’s doorstep
World.content:
JERICHO, West Bank: For years, this lush Palestinian city was an oasis of calm in the occupied West Bank. Jericho’s warm weather drew tourists year-round and its perch low in the Jordan Valley kept it somewhat isolated from the violence elsewhere in the territory.

But that relative peace was shattered this week when Palestinians said Israeli settlers who had newly infiltrated the outskirts of Jericho shot and killed a 72-year-old woman during clashes with local youth.

The killing late Monday of Fadda Fheidat came just days after the settlers had seized a cluster of Palestinian homes they said they purchased — a claim that rights groups and Palestinian residents contest.

The takeover was the first time in decades that Israelis had settled within a residential neighborhood around a major Palestinian city.

And now, as armed settlers patrol their streets, Palestinian residents say the violence has raised fears that a new phase of settlement expansion is reaching West Bank cities once considered safe from encroaching settlers.

A new chapter for Israeli settlers

Israel has occupied the West Bank since it captured the territory, along with east Jerusalem and the Gaza Strip, from Jordan and Egypt in the 1967 Mideast war. Since then, it has built a network of settlements for more than half a million Israelis on land Palestinians seek for a future independent state.

The international community overwhelmingly considers the settlements illegal. But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing government has approved more than 100 new settlements during its tenure. Settlers have also erected unauthorized outposts, which they’ve used to attack Palestinian shepherds, rampage through communities and drive people from their homes.

The seizure of the homes in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta followed a similar pattern, residents and rights groups say, starting with the construction of a new outpost nearby in 2024. The neighborhood lies just outside Jericho’s city limits, near a prized archaeological site that Israel has invested in developing as a tourist destination.

“We are writing a new chapter of Jewish life. We have returned home,” Israel Ganz, who heads the local council governing Israeli settlements in the area, declared on social media after the settlers moved in on Nov. 4.

The Israeli rights group B’Tselem described the settlers’ arrival as the latest in a series of increasingly bold and largely unchallenged efforts to drive Palestinians from their land. It warned of “a reality similar to Hebron ” — the only city where Israeli settlers have for decades lived under military protection in the heart of a built-up Palestinian urban area.

The settlers’ arrival introduces a permanent Israeli presence “with increased military deployment, restrictions on Palestinian movement, and settler militia violence and intimidation, which will affect the lives of tens of thousands of Palestinians,” the group said in a statement.

A major turning point came in February when settlers from the nearby outpost, emboldened by Israeli demolition orders for several houses on the edge of Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, drove trucks and tractors into the community and spent nearly eight hours ransacking and bulldozing homes, Palestinian residents said.

Soon after that, the Israeli government legalized the outpost. By October, settlers had taken some of the Palestinian community’s farmland and began setting up new irrigation systems.

On Nov. 4, dozens of Israelis, some of them armed, moved into eight Palestinian homes.

The settlers say they have proof-of-purchase documents for the houses, but Palestinian residents say they don’t know how, when or by whom the properties were sold.

Palestinian officials and Israeli human rights groups have questioned the legality of the sales under both Israeli and Palestinian laws. Most of the properties sit on farmland that Palestinian shepherds have grazed for generations and that Israel classifies as state land.

Under Israeli law, plots designated as state land generally cannot be privately bought or sold. Under the Palestinian Authority, the internationally backed body that administers semiautonomous parts of the West Bank, including Jericho, selling land to Israelis is a criminal offense.

A deadly clash after days of tension

Almost immediately after the settlers moved in, they began policing the neighborhood, often with guns and in ATVs, Palestinian residents said.

“They started to control our lives,” said Mustapha Fheidat, a farmer whose extended family makes up much of the population in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta. “They stop us and ask for our IDs and what we’re doing here. They prevent us getting from the main road to our farms.”

According to four members of the Fheidat family, it was one of these settler patrols that set off Monday’s deadly clash, after settlers hurled insults at Palestinian residents, who responded by pelting them with rocks.

Israel’s military said in a statement that the sequence of events that led to Monday’s shooting death were under investigation. Citing testimony collected by soldiers at the scene, it said the clash erupted after a Palestinian driver ”carried out an attack by ramming” into an Israeli settler’s vehicle as youths threw rocks at the settlers.

Fadda Fheidat was “likely injured by fire from an Israeli civilian,” the military said.

No arrests of Israelis were announced in connection with the shooting. Two Palestinian men were arrested in connection with the “ramming” incident, the military said.

Members of the Fheidat family who witnessed the violence denied the collision was intentional, saying it happened when Fadda Fheidat’s son was rushing to the scene of his mother’s shooting and skidded into the settler’s vehicle.

They said Fadda Fheidat and her daughter-in-law, Na’ima, were driving a relative who had been shot to a nearby hospital but turned back after Palestinians warned that more settlers were on the road ahead.

The violence was still underway when the women returned home. As they got out of the car, Na’ima Fheidat said she heard her children scream: “‘Grandma has been killed! Grandma has been killed!’”

Ahmed Fheidat was inside his home when he heard the shouting and gunfire. He rushed outside and found his sister-in-law lying on the ground with a gunshot to the head.

“Her skull was completely broken. My hand was full of blood,” he said.

He carried her inside to wait for an ambulance, barely noticing that he, too, had been shot in the leg.

World.title: States agree to UN talks aiming to regulate ‘killer robots’ by 2028
World.content:
GENEVA: By Emma Farge GENEVA, Nov 21: UN talks on regulating weapons with little or no human oversight ended on Saturday with a pledge for further discussions to develop new rules within two years, an outcome weakened by opposition from Russia that fell short of rights groups’ hopes.

Proponents had called for legally ‌binding rules ‌within a short timeframe to ‌regulate weapons systems that can identify and engage targets with varying degrees of autonomy, sometimes called “killer robots.”

Around 100 countries backed this position but big arms-producing nations like the US, Russia and Israel opposed this, resulting in a watered-down agreement that left ‌open the question of ‌whether future measures would be legally ‌binding. “In the end, the military powers ‌managed to impose many obstacles to the objective of a protocol, but at least it remains a possibility, and with a short-term ‌mandate,” said a diplomat who attended the talks that concluded past 4 a.m. (0300 GMT) in Geneva.

The 128 member states of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons had been meeting since Monday as alarm grows over the use of lethal autonomous weapons systems in conflicts, including in Ukraine, Sudan and the Middle East. The UN secretary-general, the Pope and the Red Cross have all called for strong and legally binding rules.

World.title: Russell, Antonelli one-two in Vegas F1 final practice
World.content:
Las Vegas: George Russell led a Mercedes one-two in the final practice before qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Friday, taking advantage of dry conditions to pip team-mate and newly minted world champion Kimi Antonelli.

Russell, who was also fastest in Thursday’s rain-soaked practice on the street layout in the Nevada gambling haven, clocked a fastest lap of one minute 34.041 seconds, 0.911 quicker than Antonelli.

British driver Russell is currently sitting third in the championship standings on 262 points, trailing Red Bull’s Max Verstappen with three races to go.

Antonelli, 20, has already clinched this season’s title to become the youngest world champion in F1 history.

McLaren’s Lando Norris was third fastest in a time of 1:35.015, just ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in fourth.

Alpine Mercedes driver Franco Colapinto was fifth fastest, 1.157sec adrift of Russell, with Verstappen sixth after clocking a time of 1:35.350.

Final qualifying for Saturday’s Grand Prix takes place later Friday.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix is the 21st of 23 rounds scheduled this season.

World.title: FBI’s criminal information database hacked, CNN reports
World.content:
The US Agriculture Department and the FBI were breached by hackers in cyberattacks, US media reported on Friday, as concerns deepened over the recent spate of tech outages at key American institutions.

The incidents were first reported by NBC News and CNN respectively, and it remained unclear whether they were related and who was responsible.

Major outages in recent weeks have disrupted travel, communications and e-commerce for countless users across the United States, even affecting a top-secret network at the National Security Agency.

US President Donald Trump has sought to calm the public and urged people to "relax", while officials said the various outages were not linked to criminal activity.

The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) told employees that a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyberattack, NBC reported on Friday, citing two former USDA officials.

The hackers may use the payments system as a backdoor to access more sensitive material, the former officials told NBC.

The USDA deals with "a bunch of scary biologic issues" and "if an adversary or a competitor were to have access to that same information... they could use our own research against us," a former official was quoted as saying.

CNN said separately on Friday that the FBI was hacked for the second time since September.

The federal agency was investigating an intrusion of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) by apparent hackers, CNN reported citing two people briefed on the probe.

The NCIC has a nationwide criminal information database linking federal, state and local law enforcement and is used to share information on warrants and background checks.

"Every day, officers across the country rely on NCIC to identify wanted fugitives, check for outstanding warrants, and access information that can directly impact officer and public safety," a former FBI official told CNN.

The former official expressed concerns that hackers "could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on."

AFP has contacted the FBI and USDA for comment.

The newly uncovered breaches at the FBI and USDA were described as hacks, which are different from outages like the ones that afflicted Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration.

In September, a hacking group known as ShinyHunters targeted sensitive employee personal data from an FBI jobs website.

The White House fired cybersecurity chief Sean Cairncross this week as criticism mounted over the string of major outages.

World.title: North Korea’s Kim visits factory sites after apparent Trump snub
World.content:
SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un was seen inspecting school equipment and teaching aids, state media said Saturday, after an apparent snub of US President Donald Trump during his Asia tour.

Trump met Kim three times during his first term and has repeatedly floated another meeting since his return to the White House, including during his Asia tour this week.

Trump left Asia late Thursday after a landmark trilateral summit which included the Chinese and Russian presidents, without meeting Kim.

The US leader suggested he was too busy to fit it in, and that he and Kim will “have that meeting at some point.”

Pyongyang has yet to comment on Trump’s remarks.

North Korea’s state media instead released images showing Kim examining teaching aids and science class equipment at factory sites.

In this photo provided on Nov. 19, 2026, by the North Korean government, Kim Jong Un (L) inspects a greenhouse farm under construction, in Ragwon county, South Hamgyong Province, on Nov. 18, 2026. (KCNA/Korea News Service via AP)

During Friday’s visit Kim “examined the samples of school fixtures of all indices to be produced by the factory,” Pyongyang’s official Korean Central News Agency said Saturday.

Science and education are the “clearest expression of our revolutionaries’ outlook on the future generations and the revolution,” Kim said, according to KCNA.

Trump had repeatedly raised the prospect of meeting Kim in China, saying the North Korean leader “would like to” meet him, despite Pyongyang remaining silent on the matter.

Kim was also seen visiting a ski resort and Mount Paektu earlier this week, followed by a naval university on Wednesday where he stressed the importance of maritime defense, according to state media.

Kim and Trump’s previous summits sought to curb Pyongyang’s nuclear program but yielded no concrete deal.

Despite years of UN sanctions, North Korea has pressed ahead, enshrining its nuclear status in law and declaring its arsenal permanent and irreversible.

Analysts say Pyongyang’s closer ties with Beijing and Moscow give it less incentive to engage Washington, complicating Trump’s efforts after his party’s crushing midterm defeat.

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: Iraq studies issuing electronic dinar to expand financial inclusion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is investigating an electronic dinar as a digital extension of the current national currency to modernize payments, increase financial inclusion, and lessen reliance on physical cash.

Prime Minister’s financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Saleh highlighted the initiative in remarks to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Wednesday, though no launch date, technical specifications, or formal issuance decision have been announced.

The electronic dinar will serve as a digital representation equal in value to the physical paper dinar rather than a new currency issue. It will not automatically generate new liquidity but will improve the management and circulation of existing funds.

According to the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), approximately 102 trillion dinars ($67.38 billion)—nearly 92 percent of all currency issued—is held outside the formal banking system.

The purpose of a digital currency is to direct the financial reserves into formal savings, lending, and profitable ventures.

Moving transactions onto official digital channels will help curb unregulated financial dealings, reduce cash-printing costs, and align Iraq with the CBI’s financial inclusion strategy.

The digital dinar plan is different from suggestions to eliminate zeros from the physical currency.

Although the CBI has expanded bank cards, digital wallets, and points of sale, it has not yet declared a formal launch date or technical introduction timetable.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb on wish list as Pakistan minister visits India; what Centre said on travel curbs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik expressed a desire to visit some of India's heritage sites, including the iconic

. Malik attended the SCO meeting in New Delhi as part of the Shehbaz Sharif-led government.

His visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India since then-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's high-profile visit in 2023 for the SCO meeting.

Accompanied by his wife and a senior Pakistani official, Malik spoke about his interest in exploring India beyond the multilateral engagement. Both are visiting India for the first time.

Asked whether he planned to visit the Taj Mahal and explore other parts of the country, Malik said he hoped to meet people and see some places if his schedule allowed.



"I have come to India for a few days. Tomorrow I will be engaged due to the SCO forum. I may not be able to explore much this time, but whatever opportunity I will get, I will try to meet people also and see some places, and understand them. People are the same everywhere," he said.

The Centre, meanwhile, denied imposing any restrictions on the movement of Malik or other ministers attending the event. Official sources said all visiting ministers were free to travel anywhere in the country, including the Taj Mahal and Humayun's Tomb.





However, security considerations may have affected the possibility of Malik visiting the Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah.

Speaking on the sidelines of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the historic Purana Qila, Malik was also asked whether the multilateral engagement could help improve

.

He said he had come to India for discussions in a multilateral context, while underlining the importance of cultural exchanges in bringing people and countries closer.

"This forum is itself multilateral. You should engage in multilateral discussions. Even the questions you have asked today have not been bilateral; everything here is happening in a multilateral context. We have also come here for multilateral discussions," he said.

Amid continued unease in bilateral ties following the April 22, 2025,

, which claimed 26 lives, Malik said culture had a "key role" to play in fostering dialogue between the two countries.

He stressed that cultural engagement was not limited to bilateral relations but had wider regional significance, adding that greater understanding between people was essential for the region's progress.

"Unless we understand each other, our way of thinking and manners of living, we won't be able to grow. Through dialogues, we will get each other's perspectives and get to know each other's understanding, and that's how the region will be able to grow," the Pakistan minister said.

World.title: 'PM-HM jodi still searching for majority': Congress takes dig at Centre over delimitation bill
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Saturday called for the existing strength and state-wise composition of the Lok Sabha to remain unchanged until India achieves the 'Viksit Bharat' goal, while questioning the Centre's approach to the proposed delimitation exercise.

He also flagged the absence of consultations with political parties, saying 100 days had passed since the 2026 Monsoon Session of Parliament was adjourned sine die without being prorogued.

In a post on X, Ramesh alleged that the government was yet to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha to pass the Constitutional Amendment Bill on delimitation.

He also questioned the lack of clarity on a fresh Bill, pointing out that the earlier legislation was defeated on April 17, 2026.



Ramesh claimed that no fresh proposals had been discussed with political parties in a structured manner and no all-party meeting had been called, despite Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge writing four letters to the Prime Minister.

Arguing that delimitation was not an immediate priority, Ramesh said the country faced more pressing economic, political, social, military and foreign policy challenges. "Far-reaching and comprehensive Delimitation can wait," he said, citing the decisions of former prime ministers Indira Gandhi and Atal Bihari Vajpayee to defer the exercise.





Ramesh recalled that Indira Gandhi had postponed delimitation by 25 years in 1976, while Vajpayee extended the freeze for another 25 years in 2001, until the publication of the first Census after 2026. Describing the two leaders as "wise and nationalist PMs", he argued that the exercise could be deferred again.

World.title: 'Rename Nagpur as Deekshabhoomi': Sanjay Raut's demand amid Dadar Metro renaming row
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader

on Friday demanded that Nagpur be renamed 'Deekshabhoomi' in honour of Dr B R Ambedkar, amid row over Maharashtra government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station in Mumbai as 'Chaityabhoomi'.

Raut urged chief minister Devendra Fadnavis to bring a proposal to rename Nagpur, saying his party would extend its support even if the move faced opposition.

"Dadar is just a station. The biggest honour to Dr Ambedkar would be to change Nagpur's name to Deekshabhoomi. The chief minister should bring a proposal and we will support it," Raut told reporters.

He said Deekshabhoomi held immense historical significance as the site where Ambedkar embraced Buddhism in October 1956, marking a turning point in the movement against caste discrimination.



"Social revolution in Dr Ambedkar's life began at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. We will stand by the government on this if any conflict arises on the issue," he added.

The demand also found support from the Congress, with legislature party leader Vijay Wadettiwar questioning why Nagpur could not be renamed after the historic site.

"The name (of Nagpur) should be changed to Deekshabhoomi. What is the problem in changing the name to Deekshabhoomi?" Wadettiwar said.





He credited Ambedkar with framing a Constitution that protects India's democracy and said Deekshabhoomi attracts visitors from across the world.

The BJP, however, criticised Raut over his demand and accused Shiv Sena (UBT) of opposing the proposed renaming of Dadar Metro station.

Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders were using the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) as a proxy to oppose the government's move.

He said Raut should first welcome the decision to rename the Metro station as Chaityabhoomi.

"He (Raut) never goes to Chaityabhoomi, nor does he propagate Dr Ambedkar's thoughts. Such people have no right to speak on the issue," Ban said.

Maharashtra minister and senior BJP leader Chandrashekhar Bawankule said Nagpur was already widely associated with Deekshabhoomi.

"Every person who comes to Nagpur goes to Deekshabhoomi," he said.

This comes after Fadnavis announced the state government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station as Chaityabhoomi, subject to completion of the necessary procedures.

The announcement had initially caused confusion over whether the proposed name change concerned Dadar railway station. The chief minister's Office subsequently clarified that the proposal applied only to the Metro station and that the suburban railway station would retain its existing name.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The renaming proposal has drawn political reactions, with the MNS raising objections to changing Dadar's name.

Both Chaityabhoomi and Deekshabhoomi are closely associated with Ambedkar's life and legacy.

On October 14, 1956, Ambedkar converted to Buddhism along with hundreds of thousands of followers at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. The event became a defining moment in the Dalit Buddhist movement.

Ambedkar died on December 6, 1956, and was cremated at Chaityabhoomi in Mumbai's Dadar area.

Both sites attract large numbers of followers every year, particularly during Dhammachakra Pravartan Din in Nagpur and Mahaparinirvan Diwas in Mumbai.

World.title: BJP in tandem with BRS to obstruct Telangana’s development: Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy
World.content:
Congress MP and Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee Media Committee chairman Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy accused Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of working in tandem with the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) to obstruct Telangana’s development and investment initiatives.

Addressing a press conference at Gandhi Bhavan, he said Mr. Kishan Reddy’s assertion that the political ‘game’ had begun was misplaced, as the game had started long ago and the BJP had already left the field and was now batting for the BRS.

He alleged that the BJP and BRS shared an agenda of creating hurdles for the Congress government and its efforts to attract investments and accelerate development. The BJP’s absence from discussions relating to the State’s progress, including the curtain-raiser in New Delhi for the upcoming Global Summit in Hyderabad, reflected its lack of commitment to Telangana, he said.

Mr. Kiran Kumar Reddy said Telangana was witnessing a significant improvement in foreign direct investment, with inflows rising from $543 million to $1.32 billion. Events such as the Bharat Summit and the forthcoming Rising Telangana Investment Summit were important platforms to attract investments, generate employment and project the State’s potential globally. Instead of extending support, the BJP was attempting to undermine these initiatives for political reasons, he charged.

Questioning Mr. Kishan Reddy’s silence on pending infrastructure projects, the Congress MP asked whether the Union Minister could raise Telangana’s concerns before the BJP’s central leadership. He specifically referred to the Regional Ring Road (RRR) and the second phase of the Hyderabad Metro Rail project, alleging that the Union Minister had failed to secure the necessary support and funds for them.

The Congress government had brought Metro Rail to Hyderabad, making it the second city in the country to have the facility, but several other cities had since expanded their networks through subsequent phases. Delhi, in particular, had witnessed substantial expansion, while Hyderabad’s Metro expansion remained pending, he pointed out.

He also questioned Mr. Kishan Reddy’s remarks about a financial emergency in Telangana, asking why the Union Minister had remained silent when the previous BRS government allegedly raised loans beyond permissible norms.

The BJP leader had neither questioned the borrowing practices nor made efforts to prevent what he described as the financial loot during the BRS regime, he alleged.

Referring to the BJP’s claims about development under its rule at the Centre, Mr. Kiran Kumar Reddy said the party was ignoring the contribution of successive Congress governments since Independence. He listed the public sector undertakings established during Congress rule and said the party had laid the foundations for India’s industrial and economic growth and placed the country on the international map much before the BJP came into existence.

He challenged the BJP to move beyond political criticism and work with the State government to secure pending projects and benefits from the Centre. He said the BJP should support Telangana’s demand for national project status for the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme and help expedite clearances and funding for other key infrastructure projects.
