The course capped off with a mock mass-casualty crisis, testing how well the medics could sort, stabilize, and evacuate patients under pressure. A debriefing followed to spot weak points and draw lessons for future deployments. /atm

World.title: Cops seize P3.4-M shabu in Cagayan de Oro City
World.content:
Police officers arrest a 38-year-old high-value drug suspect, alias “Tax,” and seize 500 grams of suspected shabu worth P3.4 million during a buy-bust operation in Barangay Bayabas, Cagayan de Oro City, on Nov. 19, 2026. —Photo courtesy of the Northern Mindanao Police Regional District (PRO 10)

CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY, Philippines — Anti-narcotics operatives seized P3.4 million worth of suspected shabu and arrested a high-value drug suspect in a buy-bust operation in Barangay Bayabas here on Thursday, Nov. 19.

In a press advisory on Saturday, the Northern Mindanao Police Regional Office (PRO 10) reported that the Regional Police Drug Enforcement Unit (RPDEU) Team 2 led the operation in coordination with other police units in the city that arrested the suspect, only known as alias “Tax,” 38, single, unemployed, and a resident of Barangay Bayabas.

Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay Jr., PRO 10 director, said in the advisory that the operation underscores police efforts to dismantle the illegal drug trade in Northern Mindanao.

Article continues after this 

READ: 4 arrested in Lucena City drug den raid

“We will remain relentless in our intelligence-driven operations and will continue working closely with our partner agencies to keep illegal drugs away from our communities,” Babagay said.

Operatives were able to confiscate one heat-sealed sachet and five knot-tied plastic sachets containing about 500 grams of suspected shabu, a white ziplock cellophane, a black sling bag, and three P1,000 bills used as buy-bust money.

Initial investigation showed the suspect allegedly sourced the drugs from Maguing, Lanao del Sur, and used a drop-off method to distribute them. Police are conducting further investigation to determine the extent of his involvement in the illegal drug trade.

READ: Anti-drug ops continue despite Asean security deployment

Article continues after this 

The suspect is currently detained at the Maharlika Custodial Facility pending the filing of charges for violating the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 (RA 9165).

The seized drugs will be submitted to the Regional Forensic Unit 10 for laboratory examination. /atm

World.title: Ako Bicol Party-list: No infra insertions in proposed 2027 budget
World.content:
Ako Bicol Party-List Rep. Jan Almario Chan —Photo from his Facebook account

MANILA, Philippines — The Ako Bicol Party-list did not request or sponsor any infrastructure funding in the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB).

Ako Bicol Rep. Jan Almario Chan on Saturday made that clarification in a statement issued on Saturday following reports from Bilyonaryo News Channel (BNC) that the First District of Camarines Sur obtained more than P10 billion in infrastructure funds in the proposed national budget for next year.

“ZERO,” Chan stressed in a statement.

Article continues after this 

“Not a single peso in infrastructure funding was requested for or allocated to the Ako Bicol Party-list,” he added in Filipino.

READ: P97-B slashed from DPWH budget in Senate appropriations bill

Chan further asserted that he and Rep. Alfredo Garbin Jr. had nothing to do with the additional P3.7 billion allegedly allotted to the district.

“We did not request, sponsor, or introduce any budget insertion related to this amount,” he said.

According to the BNC, the document they assessed came from Navotas Rep. Toby Tiangco, who obtained it from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

Article continues after this 

“It’s important to set the facts straight to prevent the spread of misinformation and the unfair association of our group with matters in which we have no involvement,” Chan said.

The P7.2-trillion national budget is under Senate review as senators and budget watchdogs flagged discrepancies in the House-approved 2027 GAB.

Article continues after this 

READ: Ejercito pushes funding for health, education, infra in 2027 budget

Among the issues raised is that certain proponents of infrastructure projects reportedly got additional funding.

“Discussions concerning national funds must be based on official documents, accurate information, and the truth,” Chan said.

The Senate finance panel, chaired by Sen. JV Ejercito, is set to sponsor the committee report on the Senate floor on Monday, Nov. 23.

World.title: Intoxicated pedestrian killed after suddenly crossing Bukidnon highway
World.content:
Personnel of the Manolo Fortich Municipal Police Station tend to the body of a 50-year-old man who died after being struck by a passenger bus while crossing the National Highway in Barangay Lunocan, Manolo Fortich, Bukidnon, early Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Initial police investigation indicated the victim was under the influence of alcohol when he suddenly stepped onto the road. (Photo courtesy of Manolo Fortich MPS)

VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — A 50-year-old man believed to be under the influence of alcohol died early Saturday after he suddenly stepped into the path of an oncoming bus along the national highway in Barangay Lunocan, Manolo Fortich town, Bukidnon.

Police identified the victim as a resident of Barangay Inutlanan, Claveria, Misamis Oriental. He was rushed to the Bukidnon Provincial Hospital in Barangay San Miguel of Manolo Fortich where attending physicians declared him dead on arrival due to severe injuries.

Initial investigation by the Manolo Fortich Municipal Police Station (MPS), headed by Police Lt. Col. Edward T. Agpalza, showed the incident happened around 1:10 a.m. while a passenger bus was traveling from Cagayan de Oro City toward Malaybalay City.

Article continues after this 

The 46-year-old bus driver, a licensed motorist from Barangay San Jose, Libona, Bukidnon, told investigators he was driving at a slow speed when the intoxicated pedestrian abruptly crossed the dark highway, leaving him no time to avoid the collision.

The impact damaged the front portion of the bus. Both the driver and the vehicle were placed under the custody of the Manolo Fortich police station for proper disposition as investigators complete their case report.

Following the fatal crash, the Bukidnon Police Provincial Office ordered local police units to step up random checkpoints and strictly enforce traffic regulations to prevent similar highway accidents, reminding both motorists and pedestrians to exercise extra caution on the road. /ms

World.title: Robredo casts vote as Naga seeks highly urbanized city status
World.content:
Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo casts her vote at the Naga City Science High School on Saturday, November 21, during the plebiscite on the city’s proposed conversion into a Highly Urbanized City (HUC). The conversion, earlier declared under Proclamation No. 1267, requires ratification by voters to take effect. (Photos courtesy of Jarvis-Ivan Sadiua)

NAGA CITY — Mayor Leni Robredo cast her vote at the Naga City Science High School on Saturday morning, Nov. 21, in a plebiscite seeking to ratify the city’s conversion into a Highly Urbanized City (HUC).

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Proclamation No. 1267 on May 26, 2026, declaring Naga City a Highly Urbanized City, subject to approval by qualified voters in a plebiscite.

READ: Marcos declares Naga as highly urbanized city

Article continues after this 

Under Section 452 of the Local Government Code of 1991, a city must have a population of at least 200,000 and an annual income of at least P50 million, based on 1991 constant prices, to qualify for highly urbanized city status.

Also, Section 453 specifies that the HUC classification requires ratification in a plebiscite by qualified votersNaga City met the requirements, with a population of 210,545 and an annual income of P298.53 million based on 1991 constant prices, according to government certifications cited in the presidential proclamation.

The HUC classification would strengthen the city’s administrative independence from the provincial government. Under the law, voters in highly urbanized cities are also excluded from voting for provincial elective officials.

The conversion will take effect only upon ratification by voters in the November 21 plebiscite. /ms

World.title: Badoc town in Ilocos Norte declared drug-cleared municipality
World.content:
Badoc, Ilocos Norte, has officially earned its drug-cleared status effective Tuesday, Nov. 17, following the approval of its application by the Regional Oversight Committee for the Barangay Drug Clearing Program. (Photo courtesy of Badoc municipal government)

SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The municipality of Badoc in Ilocos Norte has officially been declared a drug-cleared municipality after successfully hurdling the deliberation of the Regional Oversight Committee for the Barangay Drug Clearing Program (ROCBDC).

The declaration took effect on Tuesday, Nov. 17, following the issuance of a Certificate of Drug-Cleared Municipality pursuant to ROCBDC Resolution No. 006, Series of 2026.

The municipality’s application was presented before the committee, headed by Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) Regional Office I Director Julius Paderes, by a delegation led by Municipal Mayor and Municipal Anti-Drug Abuse Council (MADAC) Chairman Virgilio Calajate.

Article continues after this 

According to the local government, the delegation included Municipal Health Officer Dr. Danielle Erika Cabading-Flordeliza, MADAC Focal Person Atty. Kharizza Mae Allenda, Badoc Chief of Police Capt. Christopher Pola, and Municipal Local Government Operations Officer Ma. Beverly IBaquiran.

The recognition, according to the local officials, shows the collaborative efforts of the MADAC, Philippine National Police, PDEA, barangay officials, national government agencies and other community stakeholders in implementing anti-illegal drug programs and initiatives.

READ: PDEA declares nearly 200 South Cotabato barangays ‘drug-cleared’

The municipal government said the achievement reflects the community’s shared commitment to maintaining peace and order, protecting public safety, promoting health and wellness, and sustaining a drug-free environment.

It also thanked partner agencies, barangay officials, stakeholders and residents for their cooperation and support in securing the municipality’s drug-cleared status.

The local government called on the community to sustain the gains, emphasizing that keeping Badoc safe and healthy remains a shared responsibility. /ms

World.title: BARMM parliament to discuss 2027 budget, parliamentary rules on Nov. 24
World.content:
PHOTO COURTESY OF BANGSAMORO PARLIAMENT

COTABATO CITY — The Bangsamoro Parliament will complete the proposed 2027 budget for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) before the year ends, the parliament majority leader said Saturday, Nov. 21.

Parliament Member Johari Abu, majority floor leader, said Speaker Amer Zaakaria Rakim issued a memorandum directing all parliament members to hold a regular session at 1 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at the Shariff Kabunsuan Cultural Complex (SKCC) Plenary Session hall inside the Bangsamoro Government Center in Cotabato City.

“Top priority is the proposed 2027 regional budget committee memberships,” Abu said.

Article continues after this 

Also on the agenda are the completion of the legislative calendar, election of members of various working committees, and the parliamentary rules of procedure.

READ: BARMM’s parliamentary experiment: Can autonomy deliver?

On its inaugural session on Oct. 30, the Parliament elected its speaker, majority floor leader, deputy speakers and chairpersons of working committees, and other parliamentary officers all under MPs belonging to the Bangsamoro Federalist Party and its allies.

The Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) United Bangsamoro Justice Party failed to secure a committee leadership.

“By the first week of December, we expect that the BARMM expenditure program would be in the plenary,” Abu said, adding that the parliament eyes the passage of the proposed Bangsamoro Revenue Code within the first 100 days of legislative work.

Article continues after this 

During the Nov. 6 first cabinet meeting under Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua, Finance Minister Ubaida Pacasem discussed the proposed FY 2027 Bangsamoro Expenditure Program (BEP).

He said that, as a development instrument, the 2027 BEP will translate the new administration’s development priorities into concrete government programs, projects, and public services.

Article continues after this 

Pacasem urged ministries to apply flexibility in budget proposals, and ministers and all heads of offices may revise their proposed programs and activities, provided that the revisions remain within their respective approved budget ceilings.

A lawyer, Pacasem urged responsible budgeting, sound fiscal policies, and efficient utilization of public funds.
